terms.plain_meaning: मजबूत पर कुछ लचीला सहारा देने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: कान का मुड़कर वापस आ जाने वाला हिस्सा

unpack.example_or_place: Outer ear and joint surfaces
unpack.consequence: Support need not be as rigid as bone.
unpack.level_extra: Not every flexible body part is muscle.

p002-i17.content: Bone — child of Supportive connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What kind of tissue is bone in this tree?
teacher_understanding.answer: Supportive connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which neighbouring leaf contrasts with bone?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cartilage.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is bone comparatively hard?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mineral salts deposited in its matrix provide rigidity.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर का सख्त जीवित सहारा देने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: हाथ-पैर का अंदरूनी ढाँचा

why_chain.step: The body needs a load-bearing frame.
A mineralised matrix provides firm support.

unpack.example_or_place: Limb bones
unpack.consequence: Hardness reflects matrix, not absence of cells.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish tissue from the whole bone organ.

p002-i18.content: Blood — child of Fluid connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this page classify blood?
teacher_understanding.answer: As fluid connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which other fluid tissue is shown?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lymph.

teacher_understanding.question: How can blood be a tissue while flowing?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its cells are suspended in a liquid extracellular matrix called plasma.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर में बहकर सामान पहुँचाने वाला cell और तरल का मिश्रण
terms.everyday_image: सामान ढोता सड़क का traffic

unpack.example_or_place: Blood vessels
unpack.consequence: Tissue classification is not decided by solidity.
unpack.level_extra: Plasma is the liquid matrix.

p002-i19.content: Lymph — child of Fluid connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does the tree place lymph?
teacher_understanding.answer: Beside blood under fluid connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which major group therefore contains lymph?
teacher_understanding.answer: Connective Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does lymph connect body spaces with circulation?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lymphatic vessels collect excess tissue fluid and return it toward the bloodstream.

p002-i19.exam_note: Do not omit lymph when listing fluid connective tissues.

terms.plain_meaning: tissue के बीच से इकट्ठा होकर अलग नलियों में बहने वाला तरल
terms.everyday_image: बचा पानी वापस ले जाने वाली नाली

why_chain.step: Some fluid leaves blood capillaries into tissues.
Lymphatic drainage returns excess fluid.

unpack.example_or_place: Lymphatic vessels
unpack.consequence: Fluid balance links tissues with circulation.
unpack.level_extra: Lymph also participates in immune defence.

p002-i20.content: Simple squamous epithelium — child of Epithelial Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What do simple and squamous describe?
teacher_understanding.answer: A single layer of thin, flattened cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which lower drawing matches this leaf?
teacher_understanding.answer: The thin sheet labelled Simple squamous.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this arrangement useful for exchange?
teacher_understanding.answer: A thin single layer gives substances a short distance to cross.

p002-i20.exam_note: Simple describes layer number; squamous describes shape.

terms.plain_meaning: चपटे cell की एक परत
terms.everyday_image: फर्श की पतली tiles की एक तह

why_chain.step: Rapid exchange needs a short path.
One thin layer reduces the crossing distance.

unpack.example_or_place: Lung alveoli
unpack.consequence: Thinness favours exchange rather than heavy abrasion protection.
unpack.level_extra: Contrast with stratified squamous.

p002-i21.content: Stratified squamous epithelium — child of Epithelial Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What does stratified squamous mean?
teacher_understanding.answer: Several cell layers with flattened cells at the exposed surface.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tree leaf provides its single-layer contrast?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple squamous epithelium.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are multiple layers useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: Surface cells can be worn away while deeper layers maintain protection.

p002-i21.exam_note: Stratified refers to layers, not a cuboidal shape.

terms.plain_meaning: कई परतों में लगा हुआ
terms.everyday_image: एक के ऊपर एक रखी चादरें

why_chain.step: Exposed surfaces experience rubbing.
Multiple layers preserve a protective barrier.

unpack.example_or_place: Skin epidermis
unpack.consequence: Protection and rapid diffusion favour different arrangements.
unpack.level_extra: The surface cell shape gives the squamous name.

p002-i22.content: Columnar epithelium — child of Epithelial Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What does columnar describe?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells that are taller than they are wide, resembling pillars.

teacher_understanding.question: Which lower label shows a single-layer form?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple columnar.

teacher_understanding.question: How can this form serve the digestive tract?
teacher_understanding.answer: Columnar cells can specialise in absorption and secretion along the lining.

p002-i22.exam_note: Columnar is a shape, not automatically a ciliated surface.

terms.plain_meaning: खंभे जैसे लंबे cell
terms.everyday_image: इमारत के साथ-साथ खड़े pillars

unpack.example_or_place: Intestinal lining
unpack.consequence: A columnar cell may have further surface specialisations.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish cilia from absorptive microvilli.

p002-i23.content: Ciliated columnar epithelium — child of Epithelial Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What extra feature does ciliated add?
teacher_understanding.answer: Hair-like motile projections on the exposed surface of columnar cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which lower drawing shows the feature?
teacher_understanding.answer: The leftmost epithelial drawing labelled Ciliated columnar has projections on its upper surface.

teacher_understanding.question: How do cilia help a lining?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their coordinated beating moves material along the surface, such as mucus in airways.

p002-i23.exam_note: Cilia move surface contents; they do not make the whole tissue crawl.

terms.plain_meaning: ऊपर हिलने वाले महीन बाल-जैसे हिस्सों वाला
terms.everyday_image: एक दिशा में झाड़ू चलाती कतार

why_chain.step: Some linings must move material along, not merely cover it.
Coordinated ciliary beating sweeps the surface.

unpack.example_or_place: Respiratory passages
unpack.consequence: Shape and surface equipment jointly determine function.
unpack.level_extra: Cilia differ from microvilli.

p002-i24.content: Cuboidal epithelium — child of Epithelial Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What does cuboidal mean?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells are approximately as tall as they are wide.

teacher_understanding.question: Which lower label corresponds to it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple cuboidal.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this tissue participate in kidney function?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cuboidal cells in many kidney tubules absorb useful substances and secrete selected substances into the tubule.

p002-i24.exam_note: Match cube-shaped cells with tubules and ducts.

terms.plain_meaning: लगभग बराबर ऊँचाई और चौड़ाई वाले cell
terms.everyday_image: लूडो का पासा

unpack.example_or_place: Kidney tubules
unpack.consequence: Do not confuse cube-like shape with flattened squamous cells.
unpack.level_extra: Use shape-location matching.

p002-i25.content: Glandular epithelium — child of Epithelial Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What makes epithelium glandular?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its cells specialise in making and releasing substances.

teacher_understanding.question: Which main branch contains this tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Epithelial Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does secretion need specialised cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Producing and releasing substances such as mucus or enzymes requires specialised cellular machinery.

p002-i25.exam_note: This name emphasises function rather than one cell shape.

terms.plain_meaning: कुछ बनाकर बाहर छोड़ने में माहिर epithelial cell
terms.everyday_image: मुँह में लार बनाती gland

why_chain.step: The body needs substances such as digestive secretions.
Specialised epithelial cells make and release them.

unpack.example_or_place: Salivary glands
unpack.consequence: Epithelial tissue does more than cover surfaces.
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer that all glands release through ducts.

p002-i26.content: Human body surrounded by four tissue panels. Upper left: Muscular tissue, with Cardiac muscle, Skeletal muscle, Smooth muscle and Muscle cells. Upper right: Nerve tissue with branching cells labelled Nerve cell; the body also has Brain, Spinal cord and Nerve pointers. Lower left: Epithelial tissue, with Lining of gastrointestinal tract and other hollow organs, Ciliated columnar, Simple columnar, Simple cuboidal, Simple squamous, and a multilayer skin block labelled Skin surface and Basement membrane. Lower right: Connective tissue, with Tendon, Bone, Fat cells, and Fat and other Soft padding tissue. Lines link the examples to body regions.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this composite add to the tree?
teacher_understanding.answer: It associates tissue groups with visible forms, body structures and examples rather than showing hierarchy alone.

teacher_understanding.question: Which four tissue panels surround the body?
teacher_understanding.answer: Muscular, nerve, epithelial and connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the connecting lines be interpreted?
teacher_understanding.answer: They associate representative body regions with magnified tissue drawings; they are not routes along which tissue flows.

p002-i26.exam_note: Use for image identification and tissue-example matching.

terms.plain_meaning: अंग के भीतर काम करने वाले cell का समूह
terms.everyday_image: एक मशीन के अलग काम करने वाले हिस्से

why_chain.step: Names alone do not show how tissues fit inside the body.
Magnified examples connect familiar organs with cell arrangements.

unpack.example_or_place: The central human body
unpack.consequence: One body contains all four tissue groups.
unpack.level_extra: Do not mistake schematic drawings for exact proportions or exclusive distributions.

p002-i27.content: Muscular tissue — heading of the panel showing three muscle forms.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this panel illustrate?
teacher_understanding.answer: Different forms of muscle cells grouped as muscular tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which three forms are named?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cardiac, skeletal and smooth muscle.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these forms share a common role?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their cells generate force through contraction, though their locations and control differ.

p002-i27.exam_note: Connect lower names with upper tree terminology.

terms.plain_meaning: सिकुड़कर बल बनाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: वजन उठाते समय हाथ की muscle

unpack.example_or_place: Heart, limbs and gut
unpack.consequence: Different shapes serve a shared contractile role.
unpack.level_extra: Compare shape, control and location.

p002-i28.content: Muscle cells — pointers group the illustrated cardiac, skeletal and smooth muscle cell forms.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The red elongated cellular forms in the muscular tissue panel.

teacher_understanding.question: Which forms are compared?
teacher_understanding.answer: Branched cardiac, cylindrical skeletal and tapered smooth muscle forms.

teacher_understanding.question: How can cells generate force?
teacher_understanding.answer: Contractile proteins inside muscle cells interact to shorten or develop tension.

terms.plain_meaning: muscle बनाने वाले सिकुड़ सकने वाले cell
terms.everyday_image: रस्सी के साथ काम करते कई धागे

unpack.example_or_place: Muscular panel
unpack.consequence: A muscle is made of specialised cells, not a single solid strip.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid treating every drawn bundle as one cell.

p002-i29.content: Cardiac muscle — label beneath the branched red muscle drawing, associated with the heart region.

teacher_understanding.question: What visual feature identifies this example?
teacher_understanding.answer: The drawing shows branching interconnected muscle fibres.

teacher_understanding.question: Which organ is associated with it?
teacher_understanding.answer: The heart region of the central body.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is coordinated contraction important there?
teacher_understanding.answer: The heart must develop organised pumping force to move blood.

terms.plain_meaning: दिल की धड़कन पैदा करने वाली muscle
terms.everyday_image: बार-बार चलने वाला pump

unpack.example_or_place: Heart wall
unpack.consequence: Connects a cell pattern with an organ's pumping task.
unpack.level_extra: Do not classify cardiac muscle as smooth.

p002-i30.content: Skeletal muscle — label beneath a cylindrical bundle of red fibres.

teacher_understanding.question: What shape is pictured?
teacher_understanding.answer: Long cylindrical fibres arranged together in a bundle.

teacher_understanding.question: Which upper tree term corresponds to this example?
teacher_understanding.answer: The tree's striated muscle branch represents skeletal muscle in this introductory scheme.

teacher_understanding.question: How does skeletal muscle move a limb?
teacher_understanding.answer: Contraction pulls through attachments on bones, producing movement at joints.

terms.plain_meaning: आम तौर पर हड्डियों को खींचकर हरकत कराने वाली muscle
terms.everyday_image: कोहनी मोड़ता हाथ

why_chain.step: Bones cannot pull themselves.
Contracting skeletal muscle supplies the pulling force.

unpack.example_or_place: Arm muscles
unpack.consequence: Links muscle with the tendon example.
unpack.level_extra: Muscles pull rather than actively push bones.

p002-i31.content: Smooth muscle — label beneath elongated tapered red cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What cell shape is illustrated?
teacher_understanding.answer: Elongated cells tapering toward their ends.

teacher_understanding.question: Which muscle in the tree is also called smooth?
teacher_understanding.answer: Non-striated muscle.

teacher_understanding.question: How does smooth muscle move food?
teacher_understanding.answer: Coordinated contractions of the gut wall propel contents along the digestive tract.

terms.plain_meaning: बिना आड़ी धारियों वाली, अपने-आप काम करने वाली muscle
terms.everyday_image: खाना आगे बढ़ाती आँत

unpack.example_or_place: Walls of many hollow organs
unpack.consequence: Internal movement need not be under conscious control.
unpack.level_extra: Shape recognition: tapered ends, not cylindrical bundles.

p002-i32.content: Brain — pointer to the organ within the head.

teacher_understanding.question: What structure is identified?
teacher_understanding.answer: The brain drawn within the head.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue group is associated with it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Nervous tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the brain contribute to coordination?
teacher_understanding.answer: It processes incoming information and helps organise outgoing responses.

p002-i32.exam_note: An organ, not an individual neuron.

terms.plain_meaning: सिर में मौजूद संदेश समझने और काम सँभालने वाला अंग
terms.everyday_image: शरीर का control room

unpack.example_or_place: Inside the skull
unpack.consequence: Connects nervous tissue with an organ.
unpack.level_extra: Brain and spinal cord form the central nervous system.

p002-i33.content: Spinal cord — pointer to the long central nervous structure descending from the brain.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the pointer identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The central cord descending from the brain along the back.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue system does it illustrate?
teacher_understanding.answer: The nervous system.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the spinal cord help communication?
teacher_understanding.answer: It carries signals between brain and body and contains circuits for many reflexes.

p002-i33.exam_note: Spinal cord is not the vertebral column.

terms.plain_meaning: रीढ़ के अंदर चलने वाला nerve संदेशों का मुख्य रास्ता
terms.everyday_image: मुख्य cable से निकलती छोटी तारें

unpack.example_or_place: Within the vertebral canal
unpack.consequence: Links central processing with body nerves.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish nervous cord from bony protection.

p002-i34.content: Nerve — pointer to a branching yellow structure extending into the body.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: A branching nerve pathway extending away from the central nervous structures.

teacher_understanding.question: Which nearby label names a cell rather than a bundle?
teacher_understanding.answer: Nerve cell in the Nerve tissue box.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a nerve differ from one neuron?
teacher_understanding.answer: A nerve contains bundles of nerve fibres, with supporting connective tissue, rather than being one cell.

p002-i34.exam_note: Nerve and neuron are not synonyms.

terms.plain_meaning: संदेश ले जाने वाले कई nerve fibres का बंडल
terms.everyday_image: कई तारों वाली cable

unpack.example_or_place: Nerves running into limbs
unpack.consequence: Separate cell, tissue and organ-scale structures.
unpack.level_extra: Nerve fibres are usually axons.

p002-i35.content: Nerve tissue — panel containing several branching purple nerve-cell drawings.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the panel show?
teacher_understanding.answer: Several cells with radiating processes, presented as nerve tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which main branch corresponds to it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Nervous / Neural Tissue in the upper tree.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are cell processes useful here?
teacher_understanding.answer: Processes allow neurons to receive inputs and communicate with other cells over distances.

p002-i35.exam_note: Recognise branching cells, not muscle fibres.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर के संदेश लेने और आगे भेजने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: जुड़ा हुआ communication network

unpack.example_or_place: Brain, spinal cord and nerves
unpack.consequence: Branching is related to connectivity.
unpack.level_extra: Nervous tissue also includes supporting cells not separately labelled here.

p002-i36.content: Nerve cell — pointer to an individual branching cell in the Nerve tissue panel.

teacher_understanding.question: What is a nerve cell called?
teacher_understanding.answer: A neuron, specialised for receiving and transmitting signals.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visible feature distinguishes the illustrated cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Processes extend outward from their central cell bodies.

teacher_understanding.question: How do a neuron's processes divide communication work?
teacher_understanding.answer: Dendrites generally receive inputs and an axon carries signals toward other cells.

p002-i36.exam_note: Neuron is the cell; nerve is a bundle.

terms.plain_meaning: संदेश लेने और भेजने वाला खास cell
terms.everyday_image: कई connections वाला telephone point

why_chain.step: Information must pass between separated body regions.
Neuronal processes provide receiving and transmitting connections.

unpack.example_or_place: Neuron drawings in the right panel
unpack.consequence: Structure supports signal transmission.
unpack.level_extra: Do not assume every neuron has the exact drawn shape.

p002-i37.content: Epithelial tissue — heading over four epithelial forms and a skin-layer block.

teacher_understanding.question: What arrangements does this panel illustrate?
teacher_understanding.answer: Ciliated columnar, simple columnar, simple cuboidal, simple squamous and a multilayered skin example.

teacher_understanding.question: Which body relationships are labelled?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lining of gastrointestinal tract and other hollow organs, skin surface and basement membrane.

teacher_understanding.question: How can one tissue class have these forms?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cell shape, number of layers and surface specialisations vary with the task of the lining.

terms.plain_meaning: सतह और अंदर की lining बनाने वाले cell की परत
terms.everyday_image: दीवार पर लगी tiles

unpack.example_or_place: Skin and hollow-organ linings
unpack.consequence: The same broad class can protect, absorb or move material.
unpack.level_extra: The panel is a representative selection, not every leaf in the tree.

p002-i38.content: Lining of gastrointestinal tract and other hollow organs — text associated with the epithelial examples and the body's digestive region.

teacher_understanding.question: What is meant by lining a hollow organ?
teacher_understanding.answer: A layer covers the inward-facing surface around the organ's internal space.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue is linked to this lining here?
teacher_understanding.answer: Epithelial tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the digestive tract need a specialised lining?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its surface must separate body tissues from contents while supporting region-specific protection, secretion or absorption.

p002-i38.exam_note: Do not assign one epithelial subtype to every digestive region.

terms.plain_meaning: अंदर की सतह पर बिछी परत
terms.everyday_image: नली की अंदरूनी दीवार

terms.plain_meaning: खाना गुजरने और पचने का पेट-आँत वाला रास्ता
terms.everyday_image: खाने का शरीर के अंदर सफर

why_chain.step: Gut contents must be kept distinct from underlying tissues.
An epithelial boundary also permits controlled absorption and secretion.

unpack.example_or_place: Stomach and intestine
unpack.consequence: A lining is a functional boundary, not merely packaging.
unpack.level_extra: The label is general and does not place every pictured subtype throughout the gut.

p002-i39.content: Ciliated columnar — tall cells with a fringe of projections on the exposed surface.

teacher_understanding.question: What two features are visible?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tall cells and an upper fringe of hair-like projections.

teacher_understanding.question: Which upper tree label matches?
teacher_understanding.answer: Ciliated columnar epithelium.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this fringe work?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cilia beat in coordinated patterns to move material along the surface.

p002-i39.exam_note: Look for the fringe as well as tall cells.

terms.plain_meaning: लंबे cell जिनके ऊपर हिलने वाले बाल-जैसे हिस्से हैं
terms.everyday_image: खंभों के ऊपर लगी चलती झाड़ू

unpack.example_or_place: Airway lining
unpack.consequence: Surface movement distinguishes it from plain columnar epithelium.
unpack.level_extra: Not every tall-cell drawing is ciliated.

p002-i40.content: Simple columnar — drawing of a single layer of tall epithelial cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the drawing emphasise?
teacher_understanding.answer: A single row of tall cells forming a continuous layer.

teacher_understanding.question: Which part of the name specifies layer number?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple means one cell layer.

teacher_understanding.question: How is it useful in the intestine?
teacher_understanding.answer: Specialised columnar cells absorb nutrients and contribute secretions at the lining.

p002-i40.exam_note: Simple is not a statement about biological complexity.

terms.plain_meaning: लंबे cell की एक परत
terms.everyday_image: एक कतार में खड़े pillars

unpack.example_or_place: Intestinal lining
unpack.consequence: Read both layer number and shape from the name.
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse surface microvilli with cilia.

p002-i41.content: Simple cuboidal — drawing of a single sheet of approximately cube-shaped cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What arrangement is pictured?
teacher_understanding.answer: One layer of cells with roughly comparable height and width.

teacher_understanding.question: Which epithelial shape contrasts with this?
teacher_understanding.answer: Columnar cells are taller; squamous cells are flatter.

teacher_understanding.question: How can cuboidal cells serve a tubule?
teacher_understanding.answer: They form its lining and can exchange selected substances between the tubule contents and surrounding tissues.

terms.plain_meaning: पासे जैसे cell की एक परत
terms.everyday_image: एक कतार में रखे छोटे cubes

unpack.example_or_place: Many kidney tubules
unpack.consequence: Links shape recognition to absorption and secretion.
unpack.level_extra: The schematic is not an exact geometric cube.

p002-i42.content: Simple squamous — thin, flat single-layer epithelial drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes this pictured layer?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is much flatter and thinner than the columnar and cuboidal examples.

teacher_understanding.question: Which upper leaf is represented?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple squamous epithelium.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does thinness favour diffusion?
teacher_understanding.answer: Molecules have less distance to travel across the barrier.

p002-i42.exam_note: Flattened cells and one layer are separate clues.

terms.plain_meaning: पतले चपटे cell की एक तह
terms.everyday_image: फर्श पर बिछी tiles

unpack.example_or_place: Alveolar gas-exchange surface
unpack.consequence: Contrast with the thick skin example below.
unpack.level_extra: Not the multilayered epidermis.

p002-i43.content: Skin surface — label beside the multilayered epithelial block associated with the body's outer surface.

teacher_understanding.question: What visual arrangement is associated with skin?
teacher_understanding.answer: A thick block with several layers of cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which upper epithelial category matches the epidermal example?
teacher_understanding.answer: Stratified squamous epithelium.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the skin surface need multiple layers?
teacher_understanding.answer: Repeated friction and exposure require a durable barrier while outer cells are shed.

p002-i43.exam_note: Whole skin contains more than epithelial tissue.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर की बाहर वाली ढकने की सतह
terms.everyday_image: हाथ की रोज़ रगड़ सहती त्वचा

why_chain.step: Outer surfaces suffer rubbing and exposure.
Many layers protect deeper tissues as surface cells wear away.

unpack.example_or_place: Epidermis
unpack.consequence: Protection contrasts with the thin diffusion barrier.
unpack.level_extra: Do not call the whole skin one epithelial sheet.

p002-i44.content: Basement membrane — pointer to the basal boundary under the multilayered epithelial block.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the pointer identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The boundary beneath the epithelial cell layers rather than their exposed surface.

teacher_understanding.question: Which side of the epithelial block is it on?
teacher_understanding.answer: The basal, or underlying, side.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the basement membrane help epithelium?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a specialised extracellular layer that anchors and supports the epithelium over underlying connective tissue.

p002-i44.exam_note: Basement membrane is not a layer of epithelial cells or a cell membrane.

terms.plain_meaning: epithelium के नीचे की पतली सहारा देने वाली तह
terms.everyday_image: tiles के नीचे का आधार

why_chain.step: A cell sheet needs anchorage to underlying tissue.
The basement membrane provides an attachment interface.

unpack.example_or_place: Base of the pictured skin epithelial block
unpack.consequence: The exposed and basal sides have different relationships.
unpack.level_extra: It is extracellular, not the plasma membrane of one cell.

p002-i45.content: Connective tissue — panel containing Tendon, Bone, Fat cells and Fat and other Soft padding tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What range does this panel illustrate?
teacher_understanding.answer: A fibrous tendon, a hard bone and soft fat-related padding are presented together as connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tree branches help organise these examples?
teacher_understanding.answer: Connective tissue proper contains fibrous and adipose tissues; supportive connective tissue contains bone.

teacher_understanding.question: Why do these examples have different textures?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their proportions of cells, fibres, stored fat and matrix materials differ according to function.

p002-i45.exam_note: The lower panel does not show every connective subtype.

terms.plain_meaning: जोड़ने, सहारा देने और padding बनाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: रस्सी, ढाँचा और गद्दी के अलग काम

unpack.example_or_place: Tendon, bone and body fat
unpack.consequence: Appearance alone cannot exclude an example from the connective group.
unpack.level_extra: Remember blood and lymph from the upper tree too.

p002-i46.content: Tendon — label beside a yellow bundle of parallel fibres.

teacher_understanding.question: What visual feature is emphasised?
teacher_understanding.answer: Closely aligned fibres arranged as a bundle.

teacher_understanding.question: Which structures does a tendon typically connect?
teacher_understanding.answer: Muscle to bone.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a tendon help movement?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its strong collagen fibres transmit the pull of a contracting muscle to bone.

p002-i46.exam_note: Tendon: muscle to bone; ligament: bone to bone.

terms.plain_meaning: muscle की खींच को हड्डी तक पहुँचाने वाली मजबूत पट्टी
terms.everyday_image: एड़ी के पीछे महसूस होने वाली मजबूत डोरी

why_chain.step: A muscle's pull must reach the skeleton.
Parallel strong fibres transmit tension through the tendon.

unpack.example_or_place: Achilles tendon near the heel
unpack.consequence: Connective tissue helps muscle produce joint movement.
unpack.level_extra: Do not swap tendon and ligament.

p002-i47.content: Bone — label beside a pale long-bone drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: What example is pictured?
teacher_understanding.answer: A long-bone-shaped structure within the connective tissue panel.

teacher_understanding.question: Which upper subcategory contains bone?
teacher_understanding.answer: Supportive connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does bone contribute to movement as well as support?
teacher_understanding.answer: Bones act as levers that muscles pull at joints.

p002-i47.exam_note: Hard bone is connective tissue, not muscular tissue.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर को सख्त सहारा देने वाला जीवित हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: बाँह का अंदर का ढाँचा

unpack.example_or_place: Long bones of limbs
unpack.consequence: Support and movement involve cooperation between tissues.
unpack.level_extra: Bone hardness comes from its mineralised matrix.

p002-i48.content: Fat and other Soft padding tissue — label associated with the soft fat example and the body's thigh region.

teacher_understanding.question: What property does this label emphasise?
teacher_understanding.answer: The soft, padding character of fat-associated connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tree term identifies fat-storing tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Adipose tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is soft padding useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: It cushions structures against mechanical impacts; stored fat also serves as fuel and insulation.

p002-i48.exam_note: Softness does not exclude connective-tissue classification.

terms.plain_meaning: दबाव और चोट कम करने वाली नरम भरावट
terms.everyday_image: कुर्सी की गद्दी

why_chain.step: Body structures face pressure and knocks.
Soft tissue padding cushions them.

unpack.example_or_place: Subcutaneous fat
unpack.consequence: Connective tissues can cushion as well as form a hard frame.
unpack.level_extra: Do not interpret the drawing as the only location of body fat.

p002-i49.content: Fat cells — pointer to a small cluster of rounded yellow-orange cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the pointer identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: Individual rounded cells forming the pictured fat cluster.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue contains specialised fat-storing cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Adipose tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a fat cell store energy?
teacher_understanding.answer: It accumulates lipid inside the cell, which can later be mobilised when the body needs fuel.

p002-i49.exam_note: Connect fat cells with adipose connective tissue.

terms.plain_meaning: अपने अंदर fat जमा करने वाले cell
terms.everyday_image: बचत रखती छोटी गुल्लकें

why_chain.step: Energy intake and energy demand do not always coincide.
Stored lipid provides a reserve for later use.

unpack.example_or_place: Fat deposits beneath skin
unpack.consequence: Cell-level storage contributes to tissue-level padding and insulation.
unpack.level_extra: Adipose is a living cellular tissue, not just an inert oil deposit.

p003-i1.content:
There are mainly four different types of tissues present in our body.
1. Epithelial- provides covering or lining
2. Muscular- helps in movement
3. Neural- responds to stimuli
4. Connective- supports, links and cushions

teacher_understanding.question: Which four tissue groups does the page identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: Epithelial, muscular, neural and connective tissues are the four main groups identified.

teacher_understanding.question: How do their principal functions differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Epithelial tissue covers or lines; muscular tissue enables movement; neural tissue responds to stimuli; connective tissue supports, links and cushions.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a body need different tissue groups?
teacher_understanding.answer: A protective boundary, movement, rapid responses and physical support involve different tasks. Groups of specialised cells divide these tasks rather than requiring one cell type to perform them equally well.

prerequisites: tissue as a group of cells performing a shared function
p003-i1.exam_note: Core tissue–function matching and odd-one-out material; these are main groups, not epithelial subtypes.

terms.plain_meaning: ढकने या अंदर की lining बनाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: बिस्तर पर बिछी चादर

terms.plain_meaning: सिकुड़कर शरीर के हिस्से हिलाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: कोहनी मोड़ते समय बाँह का उभरना

terms.plain_meaning: ऐसे बदलाव जिन पर शरीर जवाब देता है
terms.everyday_image: गरम बर्तन छूते ही हाथ हटाना

terms.plain_meaning: हिस्सों को सहारा देने, जोड़ने और झटका कम करने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: पैकिंग में चीज़ को सहारा देता गद्देदार सामान

why_chain.step: The body needs covering, movement, responses and support.
Specialised cell groups divide these jobs, making tissue classification useful.

unpack.example_or_place: Connect a covering to skin, movement to bending an arm, and a response to touching something hot.
unpack.consequence: The rest of the page zooms into the covering-and-lining group.
unpack.visual_verb: Separate four jobs into four tissue groups.
unpack.level_extra: Practise matching functions without confusing neural response with muscular movement.

p003-i2.content: Epithelium covers most organs and cavities within the body.

teacher_understanding.question: What spatial role does epithelium have?
teacher_understanding.answer: It forms a covering or lining associated with most organs and body cavities.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does the page later give examples of epithelial linings?
teacher_understanding.answer: Examples include blood vessels, lung air sacs, kidney tubules, the digestive tract and the mouth.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is a lining important at these surfaces?
teacher_understanding.answer: A surface separates one environment from another. A lining can protect the underlying body while regulating exchange across that boundary.

p003-i2.exam_note: Epithelium is not restricted to the outside of the body.

terms.plain_meaning: किसी खाली हिस्से की अंदर वाली सतह पर लगी परत
terms.everyday_image: जैकेट की अंदर लगी परत

why_chain.step: Organs and cavities have surfaces that meet other spaces or materials.
Epithelium covers or lines these surfaces.

unpack.example_or_place: Follow swallowed food into the digestive tract and identify its inner lining.
unpack.consequence: Covering is a position; the particular lining may additionally absorb, secrete or protect.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish covering an organ from making up the whole organ.

p003-i3.content: It also forms a barrier to keep different body systems separate.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the page describe epithelium as a barrier?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its barrier role helps keep different body systems separate rather than leaving their contents in unrestricted contact.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a barrier still allow useful exchange?
teacher_understanding.answer: A biological barrier need not be an impermeable wall. Depending on the epithelial type, materials can cross through controlled routes while the tissue maintains a boundary.

p003-i3.exam_note: Barrier does not mean that absorption, secretion or diffusion cannot occur.

terms.plain_meaning: बिना रोक-टोक मिल जाने से रोकने वाली हद
terms.everyday_image: घर की दीवार में नियंत्रित आने-जाने के लिए दरवाज़ा

why_chain.step: Different body compartments need to remain distinct.
Epithelium provides a separating barrier.

unpack.example_or_place: An intestinal lining separates the contents of the gut from underlying tissues.
unpack.consequence: A continuous sheet is suited to separating spaces.
unpack.visual_verb: Separate two compartments with a sheet.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid the absolute claim that epithelial barriers block every substance.

p003-i4.content: Epithelial tissue cells are tightly packed and form a continuous sheet.

teacher_understanding.question: How are epithelial cells arranged?
teacher_understanding.answer: Closely adjoining cells collectively form a continuous sheet rather than a loose scattering.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is this sheet arrangement used?
teacher_understanding.answer: In the epithelial coverings and linings of organs and cavities described on the page.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does close packing suit a barrier?
teacher_understanding.answer: Large uncontrolled gaps would interrupt the boundary. Close cell contact helps a lining maintain continuity.

p003-i4.exam_note: Closely packed cells are a distinguishing epithelial feature.

terms.plain_meaning: पास-पास जुड़े cells की बिना बड़े खाली अंतर वाली परत
terms.everyday_image: पास-पास लगी फ़र्श की टाइलें

why_chain.step: A boundary needs coverage without large breaks.
Tightly packed epithelial cells form a continuous sheet.

unpack.example_or_place: Zoom into the mouth lining from a whole surface to adjoining cells.
unpack.consequence: Cell packing supports the barrier role introduced above.
unpack.level_extra: Link organisation to function rather than memorising 'tightly packed' alone.

p003-i5.content: They have only a small amount of cementing material between them and almost no intercellular spaces.

teacher_understanding.question: What occupies the space between adjacent epithelial cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page describes little cementing material and almost no spaces between neighbouring cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What does 'intercellular' locate?
teacher_understanding.answer: It means between cells, not inside a cell.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this detail reinforce the continuous-sheet description?
teacher_understanding.answer: When neighbouring cells lie very close together, cells themselves occupy most of the sheet, with little intervening material.

p003-i5.exam_note: Retain 'almost no' rather than turning it into an absolute zero.

terms.plain_meaning: दो cells के बीच की खाली जगह
terms.everyday_image: दो टाइलों के बीच की दरार

terms.plain_meaning: cells के बीच उन्हें जोड़े रखने वाला थोड़ा substance
terms.everyday_image: टाइलों के बीच थोड़ा जोड़ भरने वाला मसाला

why_chain.step: A close boundary needs neighbouring cells to remain together.
The page describes scant intervening material and almost no intercellular spaces.

unpack.example_or_place: An enlarged section through an epithelial sheet.
unpack.consequence: The tissue is cell-rich rather than dominated by material between cells.
unpack.visual_verb: Zoom into the narrow gap between cells.
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse intercellular with intracellular.

p003-i6.content: All epithelium is usually separated from the underlying tissue by an extracellular fibrous basement membrane.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the supporting boundary described below epithelium?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page identifies an extracellular, fibrous basement membrane between epithelium and underlying tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does the basement membrane lie?
teacher_understanding.answer: It lies beneath the epithelial layer, at its interface with the underlying tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is a supporting layer useful here?
teacher_understanding.answer: An epithelial sheet needs anchorage. The basement membrane helps support and attach it to the tissue beneath.

teacher_understanding.question: How is a basement membrane different from a cell membrane?
teacher_understanding.answer: A basement membrane is extracellular supporting material beneath a tissue; a cell membrane encloses an individual cell.

p003-i6.exam_note: Position and extracellular nature are important; do not identify it as the cell's own membrane.

terms.plain_meaning: cells के बाहर मौजूद
terms.everyday_image: कमरों के बाहर बना साझा सहारा

terms.plain_meaning: epithelium के नीचे की पतली सहारा देने वाली परत
terms.everyday_image: टाइलों के नीचे का आधार

why_chain.step: A surface sheet needs a stable base.
A basement membrane underlies and supports epithelial attachment.

unpack.example_or_place: Show a side section of lining, basement membrane and underlying tissue.
unpack.consequence: The epithelial sheet is distinct from, but attached to, what lies below it.
unpack.visual_verb: Lift the sheet to reveal its base.
unpack.level_extra: Preserve the printed 'All ... usually' wording without teaching an unnecessary absolute.

p003-i7.content: Epithelial cells often acquire additional specialisation as gland cells, which can secrete substances at the epithelial surface. Sometimes a portion of the epithelial tissue folds inward, and a multicellular gland is formed. This is glandular epithelium.

teacher_understanding.question: What additional role can epithelial cells acquire?
teacher_understanding.answer: They can specialise as gland cells that release substances at an epithelial surface.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the page describe formation of a multicellular gland?
teacher_understanding.answer: A portion of an epithelial sheet folds inward, producing a gland made of multiple cells.

teacher_understanding.question: When is the inward-folding route described?
teacher_understanding.answer: It occurs sometimes when epithelial tissue forms a multicellular gland; the page does not present it as the fate of every epithelial sheet.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is secretion a specialisation beyond simple covering?
teacher_understanding.answer: Secretory cells produce and release useful substances, so they do an active manufacturing-and-release job in addition to occupying a surface.

p003-i7.exam_note: Understand glandular epithelium as a functional specialisation; multicellular means many cells.

terms.plain_meaning: cell का कोई substance बनाकर बाहर छोड़ना
terms.everyday_image: मुँह में लार बनकर आना

terms.plain_meaning: कई cells से बनी substance छोड़ने वाली बनावट
terms.everyday_image: एक साथ काम करती छोटी-छोटी उत्पादन इकाइयाँ

why_chain.step: Body surfaces need useful substances such as lubricating secretions.
Epithelial cells can specialise for secretion, and a folded portion can form a multicellular gland.

unpack.example_or_place: Use saliva in the mouth to make secretion tangible.
unpack.consequence: Epithelium is not merely a passive covering.
unpack.visual_verb: Fold the sheet inward and release droplets.
unpack.level_extra: Do not treat every epithelial cell as a gland cell or every gland as multicellular.

p003-i8.where_on_page: upper right, four stacked tissue illustrations
p003-i8.content: Four separate perspective drawings show (a) Squamous: one thin layer of flattened cells; (b) Stratified squamous: many stacked layers with flattened surface cells; (c) Cuboidal: a single layer of roughly cube-shaped cells; (d) Columnar (ciliated): tall cells with fine projections on their free surface. The drawings rest on a contrasting supporting base. There are no connecting arrows or process sequence.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this figure visually compare?
teacher_understanding.answer: It contrasts the shapes and layering of squamous, stratified squamous, cuboidal and ciliated columnar epithelia.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visual features should a learner inspect first?
teacher_understanding.answer: Inspect the number of cell layers, the shape of surface cells and the projections on the columnar surface.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a side view help identify these tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: A top view alone can hide cell height and multiple layers. A side view reveals whether cells are flattened, cube-like, tall or stacked.

p003-i8.exam_note: Useful for identifying tissue by morphology rather than label recall.

terms.plain_meaning: एक के ऊपर एक कई परतों वाला
terms.everyday_image: कई तहों वाला पराठा

why_chain.step: Similar-looking surface mosaics can hide different cell heights and layer counts.
The perspective drawings reveal shape and depth together.

unpack.example_or_place: Compare a tiled floor, a stack of sheets, cubes and upright pillars.
unpack.consequence: The table's words can be anchored to visible shapes.
unpack.visual_verb: Rotate and compare the four tissue blocks.
unpack.level_extra: Shape and layering are separate identification criteria.

p003-i9.content: (a) Squamous — identifies the thin, flattened single-layer tissue drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the squamous panel show?
teacher_understanding.answer: A thin sheet made of flattened cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which panel has the flattest single-layer profile?
teacher_understanding.answer: Panel (a), labelled Squamous.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the tile analogy useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tiles spread broadly but have little height, helping distinguish flattened cells from cubes or pillars.

terms.plain_meaning: चपटे और पतले cells वाला
terms.everyday_image: फ़र्श की टाइलें

why_chain.step: Shape recognition needs a familiar comparison; broad, low tiles model flattened cells.

unpack.example_or_place: The table links simple squamous tissue to lung air sacs.
unpack.consequence: A thin profile supports the later diffusion explanation.
unpack.visual_verb: Flatten a cell into a tile.
unpack.level_extra: Squamous names shape, not automatically the number of layers.

p003-i10.content: (b) Stratified squamous — identifies the thick, multilayered drawing with flattened surface cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What feature distinguishes this panel from the first?
teacher_understanding.answer: It shows many cell layers rather than one thin layer.

teacher_understanding.question: Which cells supply the squamous appearance?
teacher_understanding.answer: The flattened cells at the surface supply that appearance.

teacher_understanding.question: How should a learner identify a stratified tissue's shape category?
teacher_understanding.answer: Use the shape of its surface cells rather than assuming every layer has the same shape.

p003-i10.exam_note: Basal cells need not be flat in stratified squamous tissue.

terms.plain_meaning: कई परतें, जिनकी ऊपर वाली cells चपटी हैं
terms.everyday_image: कई तहों के ऊपर चपटी चादर

why_chain.step: A worn surface benefits from deeper replacement layers; the image shows a multilayered arrangement.

unpack.example_or_place: Mouth lining in the table.
unpack.consequence: Layer count links this tissue with protection.
unpack.visual_verb: Stack layers and highlight the flat top.
unpack.level_extra: Read the surface shape and layer count independently.

p003-i11.content: (c) Cuboidal — identifies the drawing of a single layer of roughly cube-shaped cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What shape is visible in this panel?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells have a roughly cube-like profile rather than being very flat or tall.

teacher_understanding.question: Which panel illustrates cuboidal epithelium?
teacher_understanding.answer: Panel (c), between stratified squamous and columnar.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a cube help separate cuboidal from columnar?
teacher_understanding.answer: A cube is roughly as high as it is wide, whereas a column is noticeably taller than it is wide.

p003-i11.exam_note: Use image shape alongside the table's wording.

terms.plain_meaning: लगभग cube जैसी ऊँचाई और चौड़ाई वाले cells
terms.everyday_image: लूडो का पासा

why_chain.step: A familiar solid helps distinguish cell proportions; a die models the cube-like profile.

unpack.example_or_place: Kidney tubule lining in the table.
unpack.consequence: Cuboidal becomes a visual category rather than an unfamiliar word.
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse cuboidal with the taller columnar profile.

p003-i12.content: (d) Columnar (ciliated) — identifies tall cells with fine projections along their free upper surface.

teacher_understanding.question: What two features are shown together?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tall columnar cells and a fringe of cilia on their free surface.

teacher_understanding.question: Which panel illustrates the ciliated form?
teacher_understanding.answer: Panel (d), labelled Columnar (ciliated).

teacher_understanding.question: How do cilia differ from the cell's pillar-like body?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cilia are small surface projections; the columnar description refers to the height and shape of the cell itself.

p003-i12.exam_note: Ciliation is an additional surface feature, not the definition of columnar shape.

terms.plain_meaning: खंभे जैसे लंबे cells
terms.everyday_image: बिल्डिंग के खंभे

terms.plain_meaning: ऊपरी सतह पर हिल सकने वाले बारीक रेशों वाला
terms.everyday_image: एक दिशा में झाड़ती छोटी झाड़ुओं की कतार

why_chain.step: Material on a lining may need movement; cilia can move it along the surface.

unpack.example_or_place: Relate the drawing to mucus movement along a respiratory lining.
unpack.consequence: Cell shape and surface specialisation explain different aspects of function.
unpack.visual_verb: Wave the surface fringe in coordination.
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer that every columnar epithelium has cilia.

p003-i13.content: Fig. 6.9: Different types of epithelial tissues
p003-i13.exam_note: Caption identifies the figure; content is covered by its panels.

p003-i14.content: Types of Epithelial Tissue | Location | Structure | Function. Rows on this page: Simple squamous; Simple Cuboidal Epithelium; Simple Columnar Epithelium; Stratified Squamous Epithelium; Stratified Cuboidal; Stratified Columnar.
p003-i14.exam_note: The table continues on the next page; do not treat these six rows as an exhaustive classification.

p003-i15.content: Types of Epithelial Tissue: Simple squamous | Location: Blood vessel lining, capillaries, air sac lining of lungs, Bowman’s capsule of kidney | Structure: A single layer of flat cells having irregular boundaries | Function: Transport by diffusion and where minimal protection is required

teacher_understanding.question: What arrangement defines simple squamous epithelium here?
teacher_understanding.answer: One layer of flat cells with irregular boundaries creates a thin lining.

teacher_understanding.question: Which locations must be associated with it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Blood-vessel lining, capillaries, lung air-sac lining and Bowman’s capsule of the kidney.

teacher_understanding.question: What function does the table associate with this thin layer?
teacher_understanding.answer: Transport by diffusion and use where protection requirements are minimal.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a thin single layer favour diffusion?
teacher_understanding.answer: Diffusing particles have a short distance to cross. At lung air sacs, a thin barrier helps gases move between air and blood.

teacher_understanding.question: How is this different from stratified squamous epithelium?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple squamous has one flat-cell layer and is associated with diffusion; stratified squamous has multiple layers and is associated with protection.

p003-i15.exam_note: High-value location–shape–function matching; one layer favours exchange rather than heavy abrasion resistance.

terms.plain_meaning: यहाँ cells की सिर्फ एक परत
terms.everyday_image: एक चादर, चादरों का ढेर नहीं

terms.plain_meaning: कणों का अधिक मात्रा वाली जगह से कम मात्रा वाली जगह फैलना
terms.everyday_image: कमरे में इत्र की खुशबू फैलना

terms.plain_meaning: kidney में छानने वाली बारीक blood की नलियों के गुच्छे के आसपास की प्याले जैसी बनावट
terms.everyday_image: छोटे गुच्छे को घेरे कटोरी

why_chain.step: Gas exchange needs a short crossing distance.
A single flat-cell layer provides a thin surface suitable for diffusion.

unpack.example_or_place: Zoom from breathing lungs into an air sac and its thin lining.
unpack.consequence: Thin exchange surfaces contrast with multilayered protective surfaces.
unpack.visual_verb: Pass particles across one thin layer.
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse Bowman’s capsule with the cuboidal lining of kidney tubules.

p003-i16.content: Types of Epithelial Tissue: Simple Cuboidal Epithelium | Location: The tubular lining of kidneys, glandular ducts | Structure: A single layer of short cylindrical cells. It may have microvilli as in proximal convoluted tubules | Function: Absorption and secretion

teacher_understanding.question: What structure does the table describe?
teacher_understanding.answer: A single layer, described in the book as short cylindrical cells, sometimes with microvilli, as in proximal convoluted tubules.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is simple cuboidal epithelium found according to this row?
teacher_understanding.answer: In kidney tubular lining and glandular ducts.

teacher_understanding.question: Which two functions are paired here?
teacher_understanding.answer: Absorption and secretion: taking substances in and releasing substances.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the shape wording be understood?
teacher_understanding.answer: Conventionally, cuboidal cells are roughly as tall as wide, as the illustration suggests. 'Short cylindrical' is the book's wording, not a reason to identify them as tall columnar cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can microvilli help absorption in kidney tubules?
teacher_understanding.answer: Microvilli increase the surface available for exchange. Kidney tubules reclaim useful substances from the fluid passing through them.

p003-i16.exam_note: Kidney tubules, microvilli and absorption–secretion are key associations. Microvilli are not cilia.

terms.plain_meaning: cell की सतह की बहुत छोटी उँगली जैसी बढ़तें, जो सतह बढ़ाती हैं
terms.everyday_image: तौलिये के छोटे उभरे रेशे

terms.plain_meaning: kidney की छानने वाली इकाई में शुरुआती घुमावदार नली का हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: शुरुआत के पास मुड़ी हुई पतली नली

terms.plain_meaning: glands का बनाया substance ले जाने वाली नलियाँ
terms.everyday_image: टंकी से पानी ले जाती पाइप

why_chain.step: Kidney tubules need to recover useful substances from tubular fluid.
An absorptive lining with microvilli provides more surface for this exchange.

unpack.example_or_place: Zoom into a kidney tubule rather than the kidney's filtering capsule.
unpack.consequence: Different parts of the same organ can have different epithelial types.
unpack.visual_verb: Enlarge the surface with tiny projections and move substances across.
unpack.level_extra: Microvilli mainly increase surface area; cilia mainly move material along a surface.

p003-i17.content: Types of Epithelial Tissue: Simple Columnar Epithelium | Location: Digestive tract and upper respiratory tract lining | Structure: A single layer of columnar cells (tall and slender) and often ciliated | Function: Protection, absorption, mucus secretion and movement in a specific direction

teacher_understanding.question: What does columnar mean in this row?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cells are tall and slender and are arranged in a single layer; the row also describes them as often ciliated.

teacher_understanding.question: Which locations are listed?
teacher_understanding.answer: The digestive tract and upper respiratory tract lining.

teacher_understanding.question: What functions are listed?
teacher_understanding.answer: Protection, absorption, mucus secretion and movement in a specific direction.

teacher_understanding.question: How can cilia produce directional movement?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their coordinated beating moves material over the epithelial surface, such as mucus carrying trapped particles.

teacher_understanding.question: Should all these locations and functions be assigned to every columnar lining?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Many digestive columnar linings are non-ciliated, and much of the upper respiratory lining is pseudostratified ciliated columnar. Shape, ciliation and number of layers must be checked separately.

p003-i17.exam_note: Avoid 'all columnar cells are ciliated'. The book's location statement is broad and the table continues with pseudostratified tissue.

terms.plain_meaning: yaani लंबा और पतला
terms.everyday_image: building का pillar: लंबा, पतला, सीधा खड़ा

terms.plain_meaning: सतह को ढकने वाला चिपचिपा substance
terms.everyday_image: नाक का चिपचिपा substance जो धूल पकड़ता है

terms.plain_meaning: सतह के पार उपयोगी चीज़ों को अंदर लेना
terms.everyday_image: आँत खाने से पोषक चीज़ें अंदर लेती है

why_chain.step: Some linings need to absorb substances or clear material lying on them.
Absorptive specialisations and, where present, beating cilia meet these different needs.

unpack.example_or_place: Link food absorption to the intestine and mucus clearance to air passages.
unpack.consequence: One shape category can carry different surface specialisations and jobs.
unpack.visual_verb: Raise tall cells, release mucus and sweep it along.
unpack.level_extra: Keep columnar shape distinct from ciliated surface and pseudostratified arrangement.

p003-i18.content: Types of Epithelial Tissue: Stratified Squamous Epithelium | Location: The lining of the mouth and vagina | Structure: Made up of several layers of cells, continuously sloughed off and regenerated. The older layer of cells is pushed upwards and becomes flat. The lower layer is columnar and metabolically active | Function: Protection

teacher_understanding.question: How are the cell layers arranged and renewed?
teacher_understanding.answer: Several layers are present. A lower columnar, metabolically active layer lies below older cells that move upwards and flatten; surface cells are shed and replaced.

teacher_understanding.question: Which protective linings are listed?
teacher_understanding.answer: The mouth and vagina.

teacher_understanding.question: Why do several layers suit these locations?
teacher_understanding.answer: These surfaces experience friction. Multiple layers allow superficial wear without immediately exposing the deeper tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does regeneration maintain protection?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cell division in the deeper layer supplies replacements as older surface cells are lost, maintaining the barrier despite wear.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is it squamous even though the lower layer is columnar?
teacher_understanding.answer: Stratified epithelial types are named by the surface-cell shape; flat upper cells determine the squamous designation.

p003-i18.exam_note: High-value trap: not every cell in stratified squamous tissue is flat.

terms.plain_meaning: ऊपर की पुरानी cells का झड़ जाना
terms.everyday_image: घिसी ऊपरी परत का उतरना

terms.plain_meaning: नई cells बनकर खोई परत की जगह भरना
terms.everyday_image: घिसे हिस्से की लगातार मरम्मत

terms.plain_meaning: जीवित कामों के लिए substances और energy का सक्रिय इस्तेमाल करने वाली
terms.everyday_image: मरम्मत के लिए चालू कार्यशाला

why_chain.step: Friction can wear away cells on exposed linings.
Several layers and replacement from below maintain protection as surface cells are lost.

unpack.example_or_place: Feel food rubbing against the inner cheek to understand why mouth lining needs protection.
unpack.consequence: Protection depends on both layering and renewal, not simply on flat shape.
unpack.visual_verb: Push new cells upward, flatten them and shed the top cells.
unpack.level_extra: Compare simple squamous exchange with stratified squamous protection.

p003-i19.content: Types of Epithelial Tissue: Stratified Cuboidal | Location: Mammary glands, sweat gland and salivary glands | Structure: The upper layer is cuboid and other layers may be cuboidal or other types | Function: Protection of ducts of various glands

teacher_understanding.question: What cell arrangement identifies stratified cuboidal epithelium?
teacher_understanding.answer: There are multiple layers, with cuboid cells in the upper layer; deeper layers may be cuboidal or of other types.

teacher_understanding.question: Which glands are associated with it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mammary glands, sweat gland and salivary glands are listed, with protection of gland ducts as the function.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the duct distinction important?
teacher_understanding.answer: A gland contains secretory regions and channels carrying the secretion. Naming a tissue in its ducts does not mean that the entire gland has the same lining.

teacher_understanding.question: How does stratification relate to its stated role?
teacher_understanding.answer: Additional cell layers strengthen a duct's protective lining compared with a single-layer arrangement.

p003-i19.exam_note: Associate with gland ducts; surface cuboidal shape does not require every deeper layer to be identical.

terms.plain_meaning: स्तन में दूध बनाने वाली glands
terms.everyday_image: बच्चे को दूध पिलाना

terms.plain_meaning: gland का substance आगे ले जाने वाले रास्ते
terms.everyday_image: घर में पानी पहुँचाती पाइप

why_chain.step: A gland's secretion needs a protected passage to travel through.
Stratified cuboidal epithelium protects ducts of various glands.

unpack.example_or_place: Follow sweat from its gland through the duct towards the skin surface.
unpack.consequence: The same cuboidal shape can occur in single-layer absorptive tissue or multilayered protective ducts.
unpack.visual_verb: Wrap a gland duct in layered cube-like cells.
unpack.level_extra: Contrast simple cuboidal kidney tubules with stratified cuboidal gland ducts.

p003-i20.content: Types of Epithelial Tissue: Stratified Columnar | Location: Male urethra and lobar ducts of salivary glands | Structure: There is a layer of columnar cells present on squamous, columnar or cuboidal epithelial cells | Function: Protection and secretion

teacher_understanding.question: What makes this epithelium stratified columnar?
teacher_understanding.answer: A columnar cell layer lies above other epithelial cells, which the page says may be squamous, columnar or cuboidal.

teacher_understanding.question: Which locations are given?
teacher_understanding.answer: The male urethra and lobar ducts of salivary glands.

teacher_understanding.question: Which functions are paired?
teacher_understanding.answer: Protection and secretion.

teacher_understanding.question: How should it be distinguished from simple columnar tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple columnar has one cell layer. Stratified columnar has surface columnar cells above additional cells, so layer count must be checked as well as shape.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should 'male urethra' not become a claim about its entire length?
teacher_understanding.answer: Epithelial linings can change along a passage. Stratified columnar occurs in parts of the male urethra, not as a uniform lining of every part.

prerequisites: urethra as the outlet passage for urine
p003-i20.exam_note: Location matching is important. Urethra is not ureter; stratified is not pseudostratified.

terms.plain_meaning: पुरुष शरीर में पेशाब को बाहर ले जाने वाला रास्ता
terms.everyday_image: मूत्राशय से बाहर की ओर जाती निकास नली

terms.plain_meaning: gland के बड़े हिस्सों से substance ले जाने वाली नलियाँ
terms.everyday_image: छोटी शाखाओं से पानी जुटाती बड़ी पाइप

why_chain.step: Some passages require a protective lining with secretory functions.
The table associates layered columnar tissue with protection and secretion.

unpack.example_or_place: Trace saliva through larger gland ducts towards the mouth.
unpack.consequence: Layer number and upper-cell shape jointly organise the epithelial classification.
unpack.visual_verb: Place tall surface cells above deeper layers.
unpack.level_extra: Use two questions for identification: how many layers, and what shape at the surface?

p004-i1.content: Continued epithelial-tissue table: three rows for Pseudo-stratified Columnar, Keratinised, and Transitional epithelia or urothelium. Inferred columns: Type | Location | Structure | Function.

p004-i2.content: Type: Pseudo-stratified Columnar | Location: Respiratory passage and ducts of many glands | Structure: Similar to columnar epithelium but all the cells are not of similar height | Function: Protection, secretion and movement of mucous [mucus].

teacher_understanding.question: How does this row compare pseudostratified with columnar epithelium?
teacher_understanding.answer: It retains a columnar-like appearance, but the cells do not have similar heights.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the distinction between pseudostratified and genuinely stratified epithelium?
teacher_understanding.answer: Pseudostratified epithelium is one layer whose differing cell heights and nuclear levels suggest several layers; genuinely stratified epithelium has multiple cell layers. In pseudostratified epithelium, the cells contact the basement membrane although some do not reach the free surface.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does the book locate it and what jobs does it list?
teacher_understanding.answer: In respiratory passages and ducts of many glands, with protection, secretion and mucus movement as listed functions.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the respiratory example link secretion to protection?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mucus traps inhaled particles, while cilia in ciliated respiratory epithelium move the mucus toward the throat. This is a respiratory example, not a claim that every pseudostratified lining has cilia.

p004-i2.exam_note: Trap: apparent layering does not establish true stratification; distinguish mucus from cilia that move it.

terms.plain_meaning: लंबे cells की ऐसी lining जो कई परतों जैसी दिखती है
terms.everyday_image: अलग ऊँचाई के लोग एक ही कतार में खड़े हों

terms.plain_meaning: चिपचिपा substance जो धूल पकड़ सकता है
terms.everyday_image: नाक में जमा चिपचिपा substance

why_chain.step: Airways need protection from inhaled particles.
Mucus traps particles and respiratory cilia help carry this material away.

unpack.example_or_place: Respiratory passages, linked to mucus clearance from the airway.
unpack.consequence: Uneven cell heights must not be mistaken for multiple true layers.
unpack.visual_verb: Trace the cell bases, then sweep trapped particles along the surface.
unpack.level_extra: Use location–function matching and the pseudo-versus-true-stratified distinction.

p004-i3.content: Type: Keratinised | Location, as printed: The outer or apical layer of the cell | Structure: Mostly dead and devoid of nucleus and cytoplasm. The cytoplasm gets replaced by keratin, which makes the layer waterproof | Function: Protection against abrasion.

teacher_understanding.question: What characterises the keratinised layer in this row?
teacher_understanding.answer: The outer cells are described as mostly dead, lacking nucleus and cytoplasm, with keratin replacing the cytoplasm and making the layer waterproof.

teacher_understanding.question: What location wording does the book provide?
teacher_understanding.answer: It prints 'The outer or apical layer of the cell' rather than naming an organ.

teacher_understanding.question: How should a learner understand the location biologically?
teacher_understanding.answer: Keratinisation concerns the superficial cells of an epithelial tissue; the skin's epidermis is the familiar example. It is not a separate outer tissue layer inside an individual cell.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is keratinisation useful at an exposed surface?
teacher_understanding.answer: A tough keratin-rich outer covering resists rubbing and reduces water loss. The protection belongs to the surface layer, not to a claim that the entire epithelium is dead.

p004-i3.exam_note: Associate keratinisation with abrasion protection; do not generalise superficial dead cells to the whole tissue.

terms.plain_meaning: ऊपर keratin की मजबूत सुरक्षा परत बनी हो
terms.everyday_image: त्वचा की बाहर वाली सूखी परत

terms.plain_meaning: रगड़ से सतह का घिसना
terms.everyday_image: जूते की रगड़ एड़ी पर लगना

terms.plain_meaning: lining की खुली तरफ वाला सिरा
terms.everyday_image: चादर की ऊपर दिखती तरफ

why_chain.step: An exposed body surface faces rubbing and water loss.
A keratin-rich superficial covering provides a tough, water-resistant barrier.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside explanation: epidermis of skin.
unpack.consequence: Structure explains abrasion protection and the book's waterproof description.
unpack.visual_verb: Build a tough outer covering and rub across it.
unpack.level_extra: Flag the printed location wording; use water-resistant when explaining the biology.

p004-i4.content: Type: Transitional epithelia or urothelium | Location: Urinary bladder, urethra, ureter | Structure: Stratified epithelium, which can contract or expand as per the requirement. Cells are cuboidal when not stretched, but when the organ stretches, then tissue gets compressed and cells appear irregular and squamous-shaped | Function: Stretch readily to accommodate the different volume of liquids. Act as a barrier and have tight junctions to prevent reabsorption of toxic substances.
p004-i4.type_note: The row describes a tissue's layered arrangement, sites and functions; its stretch response is a supporting mechanism rather than the whole item's type.

teacher_understanding.question: What is transitional epithelium?
teacher_understanding.answer: Also called urothelium, it is a stratified lining that can expand or contract and change its apparent cell shape with stretching.

teacher_understanding.question: Which sites does this table list?
teacher_understanding.answer: Urinary bladder, urethra and ureter.

teacher_understanding.question: When does its appearance change?
teacher_understanding.answer: Without stretching, cells are described as cuboidal; when the organ stretches, the tissue becomes compressed and cells appear irregular and squamous-shaped.

teacher_understanding.question: How does its structure meet the functions listed?
teacher_understanding.answer: It stretches to accommodate different liquid volumes, while its barrier and tight junctions prevent reabsorption of toxic substances.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must a bladder lining combine flexibility with a barrier?
teacher_understanding.answer: The bladder fills and empties, so its lining must tolerate changing size without allowing urine constituents to leak readily back into surrounding tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Does the table's reference to urethra mean its entire length is urothelium?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Urothelium occurs in the proximal urethral region; other epithelial types line more distal regions. The table's site list is simplified.

p004-i4.exam_note: High-value pairing: urothelium—urinary tract—stretch plus barrier; flattened appearance during stretching does not make it simple squamous epithelium.

terms.plain_meaning: urinary tract के कुछ हिस्सों की फैल सकने वाली lining
terms.everyday_image: पेशाब भरने पर bladder का फैलना

terms.plain_meaning: पास के cells के बीच कसकर बंद जोड़
terms.everyday_image: डिब्बे के ढक्कन की बंद सील

terms.plain_meaning: चपटे आकार के
terms.everyday_image: फर्श की पतली टाइल

why_chain.step: The urinary bladder must hold changing volumes of urine.
A stretchable lining accommodates volume changes while sealed cell contacts help maintain the barrier.

unpack.example_or_place: Bladder filling between visits to the toilet; ureter carries urine toward it.
unpack.consequence: Shape can change without loss of the tissue's protective role.
unpack.visual_verb: Expand the organ, flatten the surface cells and keep their joins sealed.
unpack.level_extra: Separate ureter from urethra and avoid interpreting the site list as every part of the urethra.

p004-i5.content: Seven separate epithelial block drawings compare cell shape and layering: Simple squamous, Simple cuboidal, Simple columnar, Stratified squamous, Stratified cuboidal, Pseudostratified columnar and Transitional. The first three show single layers of flat, cube-like and tall cells; stratified drawings show multiple layers; pseudostratified shows nuclei at differing heights; transitional shows multiple layers with rounded superficial cells. No arrows or sequential flow are present.
p004-i5.type_note: The image is a labelled visual comparison, not non-teachable material.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this figure make visible?
teacher_understanding.answer: It places seven epithelial forms side by side so cell shape and number or apparent number of layers can be inspected.

teacher_understanding.question: Which drawings show the simple epithelial types?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple squamous, simple cuboidal and simple columnar are shown as single-layer sheets differing in cell shape.

teacher_understanding.question: How should an unfamiliar epithelial drawing be identified?
teacher_understanding.answer: First inspect whether it has one true layer or several, then inspect the shape of surface cells. Uneven nuclear heights alone cannot prove true stratification.

p004-i5.exam_note: Useful for diagram identification and odd-one-out questions by layering or shape.

terms.plain_meaning: cells की एक परत
terms.everyday_image: एक तह में बिछी टाइलें

terms.plain_meaning: cells की कई परतें
terms.everyday_image: एक के ऊपर एक रखी चादरें

why_chain.step: Similar-looking tissue names can be confused unless their shapes are seen.
Count true layers and inspect surface-cell shape to distinguish the drawings.

unpack.example_or_place: The seven adjacent drawings on this page.
unpack.consequence: Provides a visual reference for the table above.
unpack.visual_verb: Outline layers, then highlight surface-cell shapes.
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer cell-layer count merely from nuclear rows.

p004-i6.content: Simple squamous: label beneath a single thin sheet of flattened cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this labelled drawing show?
teacher_understanding.answer: A thin, single sheet of flattened cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visual feature identifies it among the simple types?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its cells are flat rather than cube-like or tall.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can a thin epithelial sheet aid exchange?
teacher_understanding.answer: A thin barrier shortens the distance substances cross, helping diffusion in suitable exchange surfaces.

p004-i6.exam_note: Identify one layer plus flattened cells.

terms.plain_meaning: चपटा और पतला
terms.everyday_image: फर्श की टाइल

why_chain.step: Exchange needs a short crossing distance; a thin cell sheet provides one.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: lung alveolar lining.
unpack.consequence: Connect thinness with exchange, not with multiple protective layers.
unpack.visual_verb: Flatten a single row of cells.
unpack.level_extra: Recognise shape and layer count together.

p004-i7.content: Simple cuboidal: label beneath one layer of cube-like cells with visible nuclei.

teacher_understanding.question: What arrangement is pictured?
teacher_understanding.answer: A single layer of roughly cube-like cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which feature distinguishes it from simple columnar?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cells are about as high as they are wide instead of being distinctly tall.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this shape support cellular work?
teacher_understanding.answer: Compared with very thin squamous cells, cube-like cells have more space for the machinery involved in secretion and absorption.

p004-i7.exam_note: Distinguish simple from stratified cuboidal by layer count.

terms.plain_meaning: लगभग घन जैसे आकार का
terms.everyday_image: पासा

why_chain.step: Secretion and absorption need working cell contents; cube-like cells provide space for them.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: kidney tubules.
unpack.consequence: Cell shape supplies a second identification clue after layer count.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid calling a two-layer drawing simple cuboidal.

p004-i8.content: Simple columnar: label beneath one layer of tall, pillar-like cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: A single layer of tall cells with elongated vertical outlines.

teacher_understanding.question: Which pictured simple type has pillar-like cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple columnar, rather than the flat squamous or cube-like cuboidal drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: How can it be separated from pseudostratified columnar?
teacher_understanding.answer: The simple columnar drawing shows a regular row of tall cells, while pseudostratified has a misleading layered appearance from unequal cell heights and nuclear levels.

p004-i8.exam_note: Pillar shape does not itself mean stratification.

terms.plain_meaning: खंभे जैसा लंबा
terms.everyday_image: इमारत का खंभा

why_chain.step: A lining may need active absorption or secretion; tall cells provide room for that machinery.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: intestinal lining.
unpack.consequence: Tall shape and a single layer are independent identifying features.
unpack.level_extra: Compare with pseudostratified rather than counting nuclei alone.

p004-i9.content: Stratified squamous: label beneath a thick, multilayered block whose superficial cells are flattened.
