teacher_understanding.answer: They have striations, unlike the smooth muscle described above.

teacher_understanding.question: Where are these striations represented?
teacher_understanding.answer: Across the orange fibres in the cardiac muscle illustration.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can an involuntary muscle still show striations?
teacher_understanding.answer: Striations result from the regular arrangement of contractile components, whereas involuntary describes control. Internal organisation and conscious control are different properties.

p006-i16.exam_note: Cardiac muscle is the crucial striated yet involuntary example.

terms.plain_meaning: fibre पर आड़ी हल्की और गहरी पट्टियों की बनावट
terms.everyday_image: धारीदार कपड़े की बार-बार आती पट्टियाँ

why_chain.step: Muscle appearance depends on how its contracting components are arranged.
A repeating arrangement produces bands even when movement is not consciously controlled.

unpack.example_or_place: Cardiac muscle in the heart wall.
unpack.consequence: Presence of stripes cannot establish voluntary control.
unpack.level_extra: Reject the statement that all striated muscles are voluntary.

teacher_understanding.question: What endurance feature is assigned to cardiac muscle?
teacher_understanding.answer: The book describes cardiac muscle as not fatiguing.

teacher_understanding.question: Does the page provide experimental evidence or a numerical endurance limit?
teacher_understanding.answer: No; it gives the feature as a descriptive characteristic and also states the heart's contraction, relaxation and pumping functions.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can cardiac muscle normally sustain repeated work?
teacher_understanding.answer: It has a strong aerobic energy supply, abundant mitochondria and a rich blood supply. These support fatigue resistance during normal repeated beating, but do not prevent injury or failure when oxygen supply is inadequate.

p006-i17.exam_note: Similar book wording applies to smooth and cardiac muscle; it is not a claim that the heart cannot fail.

terms.plain_meaning: काम दोहराते रहने पर काम करने की ताकत घट जाना
terms.everyday_image: बार-बार वजन उठाने पर हाथ की ताकत कम पड़ना

why_chain.step: Blood circulation requires the heart to keep repeating its work.
A strong oxygen-dependent energy supply supports prolonged repeated contractions.

unpack.example_or_place: Heartbeat continuing during sleep.
unpack.consequence: Normal pumping is sustained, but adequate oxygen and blood supply remain necessary.
unpack.visual_verb: Repeat beats while showing continuing oxygen delivery.
unpack.level_extra: Do not interpret 'Do not fatigue' as immunity to heart disease.

p006-i18.content: • Performs contraction and relaxation in wall of heart.
p006-i18.type_note: The line teaches alternating muscle activity over time; the heart wall is its location, not the main structural content.

teacher_understanding.question: What alternating actions are performed by cardiac muscle?
teacher_understanding.answer: It contracts and relaxes in the heart wall.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these actions contribute to pumping?
teacher_understanding.answer: Contraction develops pressure that helps drive blood out of a chamber; relaxation allows the chamber to refill for a later contraction.

teacher_understanding.question: When do contraction and relaxation occur?
teacher_understanding.answer: They recur through each heartbeat, with chambers undergoing coordinated phases rather than the whole heart remaining continuously squeezed.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is relaxation necessary rather than merely a pause?
teacher_understanding.answer: A pump must receive blood as well as eject it. Without appropriate relaxation and filling, later contractions could not sustain effective output.

p006-i18.exam_note: Connect the heart wall's activity to both ejection and filling.

terms.plain_meaning: muscle का सिकुड़कर जोर लगाना और फिर ढीला होना
terms.everyday_image: हथेली से नरम गेंद दबाना और फिर पकड़ छोड़ना

why_chain.step: A working heart must both receive blood and push it onward.
Alternating relaxation and contraction supports filling and ejection.

unpack.example_or_place: Muscular wall surrounding the heart chambers.
unpack.consequence: Explains the mechanism behind the next line's pumping function.
unpack.visual_verb: Alternate chamber filling and wall contraction.
unpack.level_extra: Relaxation is a necessary functional phase, not failure of the muscle.

p006-i19.content: • Helps to pump and distribute blood to body.

teacher_understanding.question: What body-level function is served by cardiac muscle?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its activity helps pump and distribute blood to the body.

teacher_understanding.question: How does muscle activity cause blood movement?
teacher_understanding.answer: Contraction of the chamber wall raises pressure, helping drive blood into vessels; valves help maintain the intended direction of flow.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the body need this distribution?
teacher_understanding.answer: Body cells need delivery of oxygen and nutrients and transport of wastes away. Circulating blood connects those cells with organs that supply or remove these materials.

p006-i19.exam_note: Match cardiac tissue with blood pumping, not digestive peristalsis.

terms.plain_meaning: खून को धक्का देकर शरीर के अलग-अलग हिस्सों तक पहुँचाने में मदद करना
terms.everyday_image: पानी का pump पाइपों में पानी आगे भेजता है

why_chain.step: Body cells need regular supplies and removal of wastes.
Heart muscle generates pumping pressure that keeps blood moving through circulation.

unpack.example_or_place: Blood delivery to working muscles while walking.
unpack.consequence: Cardiac tissue activity supports the functioning of other tissues.
unpack.visual_verb: Send blood from a contracting chamber into branching vessels.
unpack.level_extra: The muscle produces pumping force; blood travels through the vessel network.

teacher_understanding.question: Which descriptors does the book give cardiac muscle?
teacher_understanding.answer: It identifies cardiac muscle as striated and involuntary.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this classification differ from smooth muscle?
teacher_understanding.answer: Both are involuntary, but cardiac muscle is striated while smooth muscle is unstriated.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is cardiac muscle not under the same conscious control as moving a hand?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its rhythm normally originates in specialised pacemaker cells, while autonomic nerves and hormones modify its activity. A conscious command is not required for each heartbeat.

terms.plain_meaning: पट्टियाँ दिखती हैं, लेकिन हर धड़कन हमारी सचेत मर्ज़ी से नहीं चलती
terms.everyday_image: नींद में भी चलता धारीदार heart muscle

why_chain.step: Heartbeat needs to continue without a conscious command for each beat.
Its automatic rhythm makes it involuntary, independently of its banded appearance.

unpack.example_or_place: Heart beating during sleep.
unpack.consequence: Appearance and control must remain separate classification axes.
unpack.visual_verb: Tick striated and involuntary in separate columns.
unpack.level_extra: These are descriptors, not exclusive synonyms: 'striated muscle' alone need not mean cardiac muscle.

p006-i21.content: An orange cardiac muscle sketch shows branching, interconnected cylindrical fibres with transverse stripes and blue oval nuclei. White spaces lie between the connected strands. Beside it is a red heart illustration with coloured vessels. The tissue sketch is labelled 'Cardiac Muscle'. There are no arrows or additional anatomical labels.

teacher_understanding.question: What association does the illustration establish?
teacher_understanding.answer: It pairs a branched, striated tissue sketch with the heart, identifying cardiac muscle with its organ location.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visible features distinguish it from the smooth muscle sketch?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cardiac sketch shows transverse stripes and branching connections; the smooth muscle sketch shows unbranched spindle-shaped cells without stripes.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the tissue network be interpreted?
teacher_understanding.answer: It represents connected muscle cells in the heart wall, not blood vessels or a single continuous cell. The white gaps are spaces in the schematic, not labelled heart chambers.

p006-i21.exam_note: Identify cardiac muscle from branching plus striations, not from the heart icon alone.

why_chain.step: A heart picture identifies the organ but does not explain the muscle tissue within it.
The adjacent network reveals the branching and banding used to recognise cardiac tissue.

unpack.example_or_place: Cardiac muscle in the heart wall.
unpack.consequence: Links microscopic appearance with organ-level pumping.
unpack.visual_verb: Zoom from heart wall to branched, striped fibres.
unpack.level_extra: Do not assign anatomical meanings to unlabelled schematic gaps or colours.

p006-i22.where_on_page: beneath cardiac tissue sketch in middle-right frame
p006-i22.content: Cardiac Muscle — names the branching, striped tissue sketch above it; no leader line is present.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the label 'Cardiac Muscle' name?
teacher_understanding.answer: The orange branching tissue sketch rather than the whole heart illustration beside it.

teacher_understanding.question: Which details support that identification?
teacher_understanding.answer: The sketch combines branching fibres, transverse striations and blue oval nuclei.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the word cardiac connect the label to a familiar organ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cardiac means relating to the heart, so the name connects the tissue sketch to the adjacent heart picture.

p006-i22.exam_note: Recognise the label through organ association and cell features.

terms.plain_meaning: heart से जुड़ा हुआ
terms.everyday_image: सीने में धड़कता heart

unpack.example_or_place: Label below the branching tissue sketch.
unpack.consequence: The tissue name is anchored to the heart without confusing tissue and organ.
unpack.visual_verb: Link label, fibre sketch and heart in sequence.
unpack.level_extra: Cardiac muscle is a tissue in the heart, not a synonym for the entire organ.

p007-i2.content: Three Types of Muscular Tissue. Columns: muscle type (unheaded), Location, Function, Appearance, Control. Rows: Skeletal; Cardiac; Visceral (smooth muscle).
p007-i2.type_note: Comparison rather than generic figure: muscle types are set side by side on four explicit criteria.
p007-i2.exam_note: Use the rows for matching and correct-statement questions.

p007-i3.content: Skeletal | Location: skeleton | Function: movement, heat, posture | Appearance: striated, multi-nucleated (eccentric), fibers parallel | Control: voluntary
p007-i3.type_note: An explicit comparison row rather than merely a picture.

teacher_understanding.question: How does skeletal muscle compare with the other two types?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is associated with the skeleton, produces movement and heat, maintains posture, has parallel striated multinucleated fibers with eccentric nuclei, and is voluntary. Cardiac and smooth muscle are involuntary.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes its appearance from cardiac and smooth muscle?
teacher_understanding.answer: Skeletal muscle has multiple off-centre nuclei and parallel fibers; the other two rows specify one central nucleus. Smooth muscle also lacks striations.

teacher_understanding.question: How do contraction, posture and heat fit together?
teacher_understanding.answer: Contraction pulls on bones to move joints; sustained muscle activity helps hold the body upright. Energy used during muscle activity also releases heat, as noticeable during exercise or shivering.

teacher_understanding.question: What do striated, eccentric and voluntary mean here?
teacher_understanding.answer: Striated means visibly banded under a microscope; eccentric means away from the centre, near the fiber's edge; voluntary means movement can be consciously initiated.

prerequisites: contraction as shortening or tension generation
p007-i3.exam_note: Do not equate striated with voluntary: cardiac muscle is the counterexample on this page.

terms.plain_meaning: जिस पर बारी-बारी से हल्की और गहरी पट्टियाँ दिखें
terms.everyday_image: धारीदार कमीज़ जैसी पट्टियाँ

terms.plain_meaning: एक लंबे muscle fiber में कई nucleus, बीच की जगह किनारों के पास

p007-i4.content: Cardiac | Location: heart | Function: pump blood continuously | Appearance: striated, one central nucleus | Control: involuntary
p007-i4.type_note: A comparison row specifying shared and distinguishing muscle features.

teacher_understanding.question: Which features does cardiac muscle share with the other types?
teacher_understanding.answer: It shares striations with skeletal muscle, but involuntary control and a central nucleus with the smooth-muscle row.

teacher_understanding.question: What location and function distinguish cardiac muscle?
teacher_understanding.answer: The row places it in the heart and gives its function as continuously pumping blood, rather than moving the skeleton or controlling visceral movements.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is involuntary control appropriate for the heart?
teacher_understanding.answer: Blood circulation must continue during sleep and without repeated conscious commands. Cardiac tissue has an intrinsic rhythm whose rate can be adjusted by nervous and hormonal influences.

terms.everyday_image: सीने में लगातार धड़कता heart

Heart की muscle बिना conscious आदेश के बार-बार contract करती है।

unpack.consequence: Striations do not establish voluntary control.
unpack.visual_verb: Beat the heart, move blood outward, then highlight striations and the central nucleus.
unpack.level_extra: Reject statements claiming that every striated muscle is voluntary.

p007-i5.content: Visceral (smooth muscle) | Location: G.I. tract, uterus, eye, blood vessels | Function: Peristalsis, blood pressure, pupil size, erects hairs | Appearance: no striations, one central nucleus | Control: involuntary
p007-i5.type_note: A comparison row joining locations, functions, appearance and control.

teacher_understanding.question: How does smooth muscle compare with skeletal and cardiac muscle?
teacher_understanding.answer: Smooth muscle lacks striations, unlike both other types. Its involuntary control and single central nucleus match the cardiac row rather than the skeletal row.

teacher_understanding.question: Which locations and functions distinguish this row?
teacher_understanding.answer: The locations are the G.I. tract, uterus, eye and blood vessels. The listed functions are peristalsis, blood pressure, pupil size and erection of hairs.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these functions relate to daily bodily actions?
teacher_understanding.answer: Waves of contraction push contents through the digestive tract; contraction in vessel walls changes vessel diameter and affects blood pressure; iris muscles alter pupil size; tiny muscles attached to hairs produce goosebumps. Uterine smooth muscle produces contractions, including during childbirth.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does smooth muscle suit these organs?
teacher_understanding.answer: These organs need automatic movement or adjustment rather than a conscious command for each contraction. Smooth muscle changes tension in their walls or attached structures.

p007-i5.exam_note: Match smooth muscle with non-striated and involuntary; do not confuse pupil size with skeletal eye movement.

p007-i6.content: Skeletal-muscle drawing: one long cylindrical, unbranched pink fiber with transverse striations and several purple nuclei.

teacher_understanding.question: What shape does the skeletal-muscle drawing show?
teacher_understanding.answer: A long cylindrical fiber with no visible branching, transverse bands and several nuclei.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visual features link it to the skeletal row?
teacher_understanding.answer: The bands and multiple nuclei correspond to the row's striated and multinucleated description.

teacher_understanding.question: How should this drawing be used for identification?
teacher_understanding.answer: Use the combination of long unbranched form, striations and multiple nuclei rather than colour, which is illustrative.

terms.plain_meaning: धागे जैसा लंबा muscle cell
terms.everyday_image: एक लंबा धागा

unpack.example_or_place: Skeletal muscle in the arm.
unpack.consequence: Connects microscopic appearance with the table.
unpack.visual_verb: Trace the long fiber and highlight bands and nuclei.
unpack.level_extra: Illustrative colours are not diagnostic.

p007-i7.content: Cardiac-muscle drawing: striated pink fibers branch and join, with purple nuclei within the fibers.

teacher_understanding.question: What arrangement is visible in the cardiac drawing?
teacher_understanding.answer: The fibers are banded and form branching connections rather than a single straight unbranched cylinder.

teacher_understanding.question: Which feature helps separate it from the skeletal illustration?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its branching arrangement contrasts with the unbranched skeletal fiber.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is a connected arrangement useful in heart muscle?
teacher_understanding.answer: Connected cardiac cells help spread excitation and coordinate contractions needed for pumping.

p007-i7.exam_note: Branching plus striations suggests cardiac muscle.

p007-i8.content: Visceral (smooth muscle) drawing: an elongated spindle-shaped pink cell with tapered ends and one central purple nucleus; transverse striations are absent.

teacher_understanding.question: What shape identifies the smooth-muscle cell?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is broadest near the middle and tapers at both ends, with a nucleus near the centre.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visible feature contrasts with the other muscle drawings?
teacher_understanding.answer: It has no visible transverse bands.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a learner remember spindle shape?
teacher_understanding.answer: Picture a long grain or a rolling pin that narrows towards both ends; do not interpret smooth as meaning unable to contract.

p007-i9.content: Five connective-tissue drawings: (a) types of blood cells, showing different white blood corpuscles and platelets; (b) compact bone, with concentric rings around Haversian canals, canaliculi and a red blood corpuscle; (c) hyaline cartilage, with chondrocytes in hyaline matrix; (d) areolar tissue, with reticular fiber, fibroblast, macrophage, collagen fiber, mast cell and plasma cell; (e) adipose tissue, with fat droplets and nuclei in adipocytes. Leader lines identify the parts; these are parallel examples, not stages of a sequence.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the lower-left panel bring together?
teacher_understanding.answer: It presents blood cells, compact bone, hyaline cartilage, areolar tissue and adipose tissue as examples of connective tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visual clues distinguish these examples?
teacher_understanding.answer: Blood shows separate cells, bone concentric rings and canals, cartilage cells within matrix, areolar tissue a loose mixture of fibers and cells, and adipose tissue large fat-filled cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can these different-looking tissues belong to one broad category?
teacher_understanding.answer: Connective tissues contain cells associated with an extracellular matrix. The matrix can be fluid in blood, firm in cartilage or mineralised in bone, giving different supporting, transporting and storage roles.

p007-i9.exam_note: Blood, bone, cartilage, areolar and adipose are connective-tissue examples despite different appearances.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर में जोड़ने, सहारा देने, भरने या सामान पहुँचाने वाले tissue का समूह
terms.everyday_image: एक घर में ढाँचा, भराव और सामान पहुँचाने के अलग साधन

why_chain.step: शरीर को सिर्फ ढकने वाली layer नहीं, सहारा, भराव और transport भी चाहिए।
अलग matrix वाले connective tissues इन अलग जरूरतों को पूरा करते हैं।

unpack.example_or_place: Blood in vessels, bone in the skeleton, cartilage at joints, loose tissue beneath skin, and body fat.
unpack.consequence: A connective tissue need not look like a tough solid connector.
unpack.visual_verb: Zoom across the five tissues and contrast their matrices.
unpack.level_extra: Use tissue–cell matching and the blood-as-connective-tissue conceptual trap.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the grouping label identify?

teacher_understanding.question: Which named examples occur within the group?
teacher_understanding.answer: Neutrophil, eosinophil, basophil, lymphocyte and monocyte.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are different white blood cells useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: Body defence requires different responses, such as engulfing material, producing immune responses and participating in inflammation.

p007-i11.exam_note: Distinguish WBC types from platelets and red blood cells.

teacher_understanding.question: How does cytoplasm support cell activity?
teacher_understanding.answer: It contains cell components and provides the medium for many chemical reactions.

teacher_understanding.question: Which blood components in this illustration should not be confused with a nucleus?
teacher_understanding.answer: Platelets are separate small blood components, not detached nuclei.

teacher_understanding.answer: Its shape, including whether it is rounded or lobed, helps distinguish white-cell types under a microscope.

p007-i14.content: Neutrophil (polymorphonuclear leucocyte) — names the illustrated white blood cell with a lobed nucleus.

teacher_understanding.answer: A neutrophil, also labelled polymorphonuclear leucocyte, among the white blood corpuscles.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visible feature supports the long descriptive name?
teacher_understanding.answer: The nuclear structure appears divided into connected lobes.

teacher_understanding.question: How should polymorphonuclear be understood?
teacher_understanding.answer: It refers to a variably lobed nucleus, not several separate nuclei; neutrophils help defence by engulfing microbes and debris.

teacher_understanding.answer: One of the illustrated types of white blood corpuscles.

teacher_understanding.question: Which blood-cell category contains eosinophils?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are white blood cells rather than red blood cells or platelets.

teacher_understanding.question: How can this unfamiliar name be linked to health?
teacher_understanding.answer: Eosinophils participate in responses to parasites and in allergic conditions; their count may appear in a differential blood count.

p007-i15.exam_note: Recognise as a WBC; detailed staining is beyond the page.

p007-i16.content: Basophil — names the rightmost white blood cell in the upper row.

teacher_understanding.question: Which other labelled cell should not be confused with it?
teacher_understanding.answer: The mast cell is separately labelled in the areolar-tissue panel, not in this blood-cell position.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a basophil contribute to defence?
teacher_understanding.answer: It releases substances involved in inflammatory and allergic responses.

p007-i16.exam_note: Identify category and distinguish it from tissue mast cells.

p007-i17.content: Lymphocyte — names the lower-left white blood cell.

teacher_understanding.answer: A prominent dark nucleus occupies much of the cell drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: How do lymphocytes connect with immunity?
teacher_understanding.answer: B and T lymphocytes contribute to specific immune responses; B cells can develop into antibody-producing plasma cells.

p007-i17.exam_note: Connect lymphocytes with immunity; plasma cells occur elsewhere in this figure.

teacher_understanding.answer: Monocytes circulating in blood can enter tissues and differentiate into macrophages that engulf microbes and debris.

p007-i19.content: Platelets — points to the small clustered blood components beside the white blood cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the platelets label point to?
teacher_understanding.answer: The much smaller clustered components next to the larger white blood cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which blood component is chiefly associated with forming an initial plug at injury?
teacher_understanding.answer: Platelets help form a plug and support clotting.

teacher_understanding.question: How does that protect the body?
teacher_understanding.answer: Platelets adhere and aggregate at a damaged vessel, helping limit blood loss while the clotting system stabilises the seal.

p007-i19.exam_note: Platelets are cell fragments, not WBCs.

Platelets चोट पर जमा होकर शुरुआती plug बनाते हैं।

unpack.example_or_place: A small cut that stops bleeding.
unpack.consequence: Blood components have distinct defence, transport and clotting jobs.
unpack.visual_verb: Cluster small platelets at a vessel break.

p007-i20.content: Haversian canal (contains blood vessels and nerve fibres) — points to the central canal within the concentric compact-bone structure.

teacher_understanding.question: What occupies the labelled canal?
teacher_understanding.answer: Blood vessels and nerve fibres occur in the Haversian canal at the centre of the ringed bone unit.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue contains this labelled structure?
teacher_understanding.answer: Compact bone, subfigure (b).

teacher_understanding.question: Why does hard bone need canals?
teacher_understanding.answer: Bone contains living cells that need nutrients and oxygen. Vessels within canals bring supplies through tissue whose mineralised matrix cannot simply be traversed by large vessels everywhere.

p007-i20.exam_note: Haversian canal–compact bone–blood vessels and nerves is a matching combination.

terms.plain_meaning: compact bone के अंदर blood vessels और nerves के गुजरने की नली

भीतर के canals blood vessels को रास्ता देते हैं।

unpack.level_extra: Distinguish central canal from smaller canaliculi.

p007-i21.content: Canaliculus (contains slender process of bone cell or osteocyte) — points to a fine channel in the compact-bone matrix.

teacher_understanding.question: What does a canaliculus contain according to the label?
teacher_understanding.answer: A slender process of a bone cell, also called an osteocyte.

teacher_understanding.question: Which contrast separates it from the Haversian canal?
teacher_understanding.answer: The canaliculus contains a fine osteocyte process, whereas the Haversian canal contains blood vessels and nerve fibres.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these fine channels help bone cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: They accommodate cell processes and support communication and exchange between osteocytes and the nearby nutrient supply.

p007-i21.exam_note: Do not put blood vessels inside each canaliculus.

terms.everyday_image: मुख्य सड़क से निकलती पतली गली

terms.everyday_image: पतली उँगली जैसा बढ़ा हिस्सा

unpack.example_or_place: Fine channels between bone cells in compact bone.

unpack.visual_verb: Branch fine channels away from the central canal.

p007-i22.content: Red blood corpuscle — points to the small blood-cell illustration below the compact-bone units.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this separate label name?

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue does this cell belong to?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a blood component, not an osteocyte belonging to the bone matrix.

teacher_understanding.question: How do red blood cells support living bone?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their haemoglobin carries oxygen in blood flowing through bone vessels, supporting the needs of living bone cells.

p007-i22.exam_note: Distinguish red blood corpuscles from bone cells.

terms.plain_meaning: blood का oxygen ले जाने वाला cell
terms.everyday_image: oxygen पहुँचाने वाली छोटी delivery गाड़ी

unpack.consequence: A cell drawn next to bone is not necessarily a bone cell.
unpack.visual_verb: Place the red cell within a bone blood vessel.
unpack.level_extra: RBC is a blood component even when illustrated beside another tissue.

p007-i23.content: Chondrocyte — points to a cartilage cell within the hyaline cartilage drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the labelled chondrocyte?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cell identified within the hyaline cartilage panel.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue–cell pairing does this establish?
teacher_understanding.answer: Hyaline cartilage contains chondrocytes.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a chondrocyte relate to the surrounding matrix?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a living cartilage cell that maintains the surrounding extracellular matrix rather than being the matrix itself.

terms.plain_meaning: cartilage का cell
terms.everyday_image: जेली जैसे भराव में बैठा छोटा cell

unpack.example_or_place: Hyaline cartilage, such as cartilage covering joint surfaces.
unpack.consequence: Identifies the living cell separately from its surroundings.
unpack.visual_verb: Circle the cartilage cell, then shade the surrounding matrix.
unpack.level_extra: Practise tissue–cell matching rather than isolated spelling.

p007-i24.content: Hyaline matrix — points to the material surrounding the chondrocytes.

teacher_understanding.question: What region is called the hyaline matrix?
teacher_understanding.answer: The surrounding material outside the chondrocytes in the cartilage drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: Which part is the cell rather than the matrix?
teacher_understanding.answer: The separately labelled chondrocyte is the cell.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the matrix important for cartilage?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its firm, water-rich material provides support and resistance to compression while remaining more flexible than mineralised bone.

p007-i24.exam_note: Matrix lies outside cells; hyaline means glassy in appearance.

terms.plain_meaning: cartilage cells के आसपास का चिकना, glass जैसा दिखने वाला भराव
terms.everyday_image: फल के टुकड़ों के आसपास जमी jelly

why_chain.step: Joint जैसे स्थानों पर दबाव सहने वाला सहारा चाहिए।
Cartilage का matrix कुछ लचीलापन रखते हुए दबाव सहने में मदद करता है।

unpack.example_or_place: Cartilage at joint surfaces.
unpack.consequence: Matrix properties help determine tissue function.
unpack.visual_verb: Press gently on the matrix and show recovery.
unpack.level_extra: Hyaline is an appearance term, not a claim that cartilage is made of glass.

p007-i25.content: Reticular fiber — points to fine branching fibers in the areolar-tissue illustration.

teacher_understanding.question: What does reticular fiber identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: A fine fiber component among the cells and fibers of the areolar panel.

teacher_understanding.question: Which other fiber is separately named?
teacher_understanding.answer: Collagen fiber is another labelled fiber component.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a reticular arrangement help tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: A fine branching network provides a supporting mesh for cells; reticular means net-like.

p007-i25.exam_note: Recognise a fiber, not a cell.

terms.plain_meaning: बारीक जाल बनाने वाला fiber
terms.everyday_image: पतली जाली का सहारा

unpack.example_or_place: The connective-tissue mesh shown in panel (d).
unpack.consequence: The tissue contains supporting material as well as cells.
unpack.level_extra: Contrast a fiber label with fibroblast, a cell label.

p007-i26.content: Fibroblast — points to the elongated cell in the areolar-tissue drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: What structure is labelled fibroblast?
teacher_understanding.answer: An elongated cell among the fibers of areolar tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which named components are not cells like the fibroblast?
teacher_understanding.answer: Reticular fiber and collagen fiber are labelled fibers rather than cells.

teacher_understanding.question: How do fibroblasts help connective tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: They produce extracellular matrix components, including collagen, and contribute to tissue repair.

p007-i26.exam_note: Fibroblast produces matrix; it is not itself a collagen fiber.

terms.plain_meaning: connective tissue का भराव और fibers बनाने वाला cell
terms.everyday_image: जाल के धागे बनाने वाला कारीगर

unpack.example_or_place: Loose connective tissue; healing of a cut.
unpack.consequence: Cells manufacture the surrounding supportive material.
unpack.visual_verb: Show fibers appearing around the fibroblast.
unpack.level_extra: Separate producer cell from its extracellular products.

p007-i27.content: Macrophage — points to an irregular cell in the areolar-tissue drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: What does macrophage identify in this panel?
teacher_understanding.answer: A cell within the mixture of areolar connective-tissue cells and fibers.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue panel contains this label?
teacher_understanding.answer: The areolar-tissue panel, subfigure (d).

teacher_understanding.question: How does a macrophage protect tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: It engulfs and digests microbes and cellular debris, helping local defence and clean-up.

p007-i27.exam_note: Macrophage is a phagocytic defence cell, not a fiber.

terms.plain_meaning: microbes और टूटे हिस्सों को निगलकर साफ करने वाला cell
terms.everyday_image: कचरा समेटकर अंदर लेने वाला सफाईकर्मी

why_chain.step: Tissue में microbes या टूटे cells जमा हो सकते हैं।
Macrophage उन्हें engulf करके सफाई और defence में मदद करता है।

unpack.example_or_place: Loose connective tissue beneath the skin.
unpack.consequence: Connective tissue also provides local defence.
unpack.visual_verb: Engulf a particle within the cell.
unpack.level_extra: Link to the monocyte illustration without calling the two labels identical.

p007-i28.content: Collagen fiber — points to a prominent fiber in the areolar-tissue drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: What does collagen fiber name?
teacher_understanding.answer: One of the fiber components drawn among the areolar-tissue cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which nearby label names a cell rather than this fiber?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fibroblast names a cell; collagen fiber names an extracellular structure.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is collagen useful in connective tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Collagen provides tensile strength, helping tissue resist pulling forces.

p007-i28.exam_note: Collagen is associated with strength against pulling.

terms.plain_meaning: खींचने पर मजबूती देने वाला protein fiber
terms.everyday_image: खींचाव सहने वाली मजबूत रस्सी

unpack.example_or_place: Connective tissue beneath the skin.
unpack.consequence: Matrix fibers contribute mechanical strength.
unpack.level_extra: Strength is not the same property as unrestricted stretchiness.

p007-i29.content: Mast cell — points to the rounded cell near the bottom of the areolar-tissue illustration.

teacher_understanding.question: What is labelled mast cell?
teacher_understanding.answer: A distinct cell type in the areolar-tissue illustration.

teacher_understanding.question: Which panel contains it rather than the circulating blood-cell group?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is labelled in areolar tissue, subfigure (d).

teacher_understanding.question: How do mast cells link to everyday allergic reactions?
teacher_understanding.answer: They release mediators such as histamine that can contribute to swelling, redness and itching.

p007-i29.exam_note: Mast cell–histamine is a useful functional association.

terms.plain_meaning: tissue में ऐसे signals छोड़ने वाला cell जो allergy और inflammation में भाग लें
terms.everyday_image: खतरे पर alarm छोड़ने वाला चौकीदार

unpack.example_or_place: Connective tissue involved in skin allergy.
unpack.consequence: Local tissue cells can trigger visible inflammatory changes.
unpack.visual_verb: Release small signal dots around the cell.
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse mast cells with plasma cells or basophils.

p007-i30.content: Plasma cell — points to the cell on the right side of the areolar-tissue drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: What does plasma cell name in this drawing?
teacher_understanding.answer: A labelled cell among the components of areolar connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which meaning of plasma must be kept separate?
teacher_understanding.answer: A plasma cell is a cell; blood plasma is the fluid part of blood.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a plasma cell contribute to defence?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a differentiated B lymphocyte specialised for secreting antibodies.

p007-i30.exam_note: Plasma cell does not mean blood plasma.

terms.plain_meaning: antibodies बनाकर छोड़ने वाला defence cell
terms.everyday_image: खास target के लिए सुरक्षा उपकरण बनाने की छोटी factory

unpack.example_or_place: Connective tissue and immune responses.
unpack.consequence: Links connective-tissue cells with antibody-mediated immunity.
unpack.visual_verb: Release antibody shapes from the cell.
unpack.level_extra: Contrast plasma cell with blood plasma and connect it to B lymphocytes.

p007-i31.content: Fat droplet — points to the large pale fat-containing region inside an adipocyte.

teacher_understanding.question: What occupies the large pale region in the adipose drawing?
teacher_understanding.answer: The labelled fat droplet within an adipocyte.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue panel contains the fat droplet?
teacher_understanding.answer: Adipose tissue, subfigure (e).

teacher_understanding.question: Why store fat in these cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Stored fat provides an energy reserve and adipose tissue contributes cushioning and thermal insulation.

p007-i31.exam_note: Fat is stored inside adipocytes, not merely between them.

terms.plain_meaning: cell के अंदर जमा fat का बड़ा हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: भंडार में रखा energy का reserve

why_chain.step: शरीर को बाद में इस्तेमाल के लिए energy बचानी पड़ती है।
Adipocytes fat जमा करके यह reserve रखते हैं।

unpack.example_or_place: Body fat beneath the skin.
unpack.consequence: Large stored droplets dominate the cell's appearance.
unpack.visual_verb: Fill the cell with a growing fat droplet.
unpack.level_extra: Adipose tissue also has useful normal functions; it is not merely unwanted weight.

p007-i32.content: Nucleus — points to the small dark structure near the edge of an adipocyte.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is the nucleus shown in the adipose cell?
teacher_understanding.answer: Near the cell's edge beside the large fat-containing region.

teacher_understanding.question: Which labelled feature takes up much more space than the nucleus?
teacher_understanding.answer: The fat droplet occupies the large pale region.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the nucleus displaced towards the edge?
teacher_understanding.answer: In a typical white adipocyte, a large lipid droplet occupies most of the cell and pushes the nucleus and cytoplasm towards the periphery.

p007-i32.exam_note: A peripheral nucleus helps identify a typical fat cell.

terms.plain_meaning: fat cell में किनारे की ओर दिखता genetic जानकारी वाला हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: बड़े सामान के आने से किनारे खिसकी मेज़

unpack.example_or_place: Typical white adipocyte.
unpack.consequence: Stored material can alter the position of cell components.
unpack.visual_verb: Expand the droplet and shift the nucleus outward.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid applying this one-droplet appearance to every adipose-cell subtype.

p007-i33.content: Adipocytes — names the fat-containing cells in the adipose-tissue panel.

teacher_understanding.question: What are the cells labelled adipocytes?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cells containing fat droplets and nuclei in the adipose-tissue drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue–cell pair follows from the panel?
teacher_understanding.answer: Adipose tissue contains adipocytes.

teacher_understanding.question: How can the tissue and cell names be remembered together?
teacher_understanding.answer: Both share adipo-, referring to fat; adipocyte names the cell, while adipose tissue names the tissue made up largely of such cells.

p007-i33.exam_note: Adipocyte–adipose is a core matching pair.

terms.plain_meaning: fat जमा करने वाले cells
terms.everyday_image: छोटे-छोटे storage bags का समूह

unpack.example_or_place: Subcutaneous fat and fat around some organs.
unpack.consequence: Connects the cell name to the tissue and storage role.
unpack.level_extra: Contrast adipocyte, chondrocyte and osteocyte in matching questions.

p007-i34.content: How do neurons transmit impulses (send message to other cells)?

teacher_understanding.question: What question does the neuron panel ask?
teacher_understanding.answer: It asks how a neuron carries an impulse and communicates a message to another cell.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the diagram begin to answer it?
teacher_understanding.answer: It shows connected neurons, dendrites, cell bodies, axons, axon tips, synapses and an electrical-signal arrow along an axon.

teacher_understanding.question: How is the message passed in a typical chemical synapse?
teacher_understanding.answer: An impulse reaching the axon terminal triggers neurotransmitter release; the transmitter crosses the small gap and acts on the receiving cell.

p007-i34.exam_note: Explanatory figure question, not a printed multiple-choice exercise.

p007-i35.content: Neuron communication diagram: an axon of a previous neuron approaches the left neuron's dendritic region at a circled synapse. The left neuron has dendrites, a neuron cell body and nucleus. Its long red axon curves to axon tips near the second neuron's dendrites, where another synapse is circled. A blue arrow labelled electrical signal runs along the first neuron's axon towards the second neuron. The second neuron also has a labelled neuron cell body and nucleus.

teacher_understanding.question: What overall connection does the illustration show?
teacher_understanding.answer: A previous neuron's axon reaches the first neuron, whose axon then approaches the dendrites of a second neuron through another synaptic junction.

teacher_understanding.question: Which route is indicated for the electrical signal?
teacher_understanding.answer: The arrow follows the first neuron's axon from the cell-body side towards its tips near the next neuron.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the typical route through a neuron be understood?
teacher_understanding.answer: Incoming signals are commonly received by dendrites and the cell body; if sufficient excitation is produced, an impulse is initiated near the start of the axon and travels towards the terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are synapses important in a chain of neurons?
teacher_understanding.answer: They provide sites at which one cell influences another, allowing messages to be passed and modified rather than treating the nervous system as one uninterrupted cell.

p007-i35.exam_note: Identify signal direction and distinguish within-neuron conduction from between-cell transmission.

terms.plain_meaning: neuron में आगे बढ़ने वाले तेज electrical संदेश
terms.everyday_image: एक सिरे से दूसरे सिरे तक पहुँचता सूचना signal

why_chain.step: शरीर के दूर हिस्सों तक सूचना जल्दी पहुँचानी होती है।
Neurons अपने axon से impulse पहुँचाते हैं और synapse पर अगली cell को message देते हैं।

unpack.example_or_place: A chain of neurons carrying information during a response to touch.
unpack.consequence: Information can travel across successive cells without their cytoplasm becoming one continuous compartment.
unpack.visual_verb: Receive, conduct along the axon, then transfer across the synapse.
unpack.level_extra: The blue arrow is an electrical signal within the axon; typical chemical transmission across a synapse uses neurotransmitters.

p007-i36.content: axon of previous neuron — points to the incoming axon approaching the first neuron's dendritic region.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the incoming structure belong to?
teacher_understanding.answer: It belongs to a previous neuron rather than to the cell body shown beside it.

teacher_understanding.question: Which connection does it approach?
teacher_understanding.answer: The circled synapse at the first neuron's receiving region.

teacher_understanding.question: How does it contribute to the next neuron's activity?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its terminal can release a transmitter at a chemical synapse, changing the receiving neuron's electrical state.

p007-i36.exam_note: Trace cell ownership: an incoming axon is not the receiving neuron's dendrite.

terms.plain_meaning: message की कड़ी में इससे पहले वाला neuron
terms.everyday_image: relay में पीछे से message देने वाला साथी

unpack.example_or_place: Incoming link at the left edge of the diagram.
unpack.consequence: Makes the drawing a segment of a longer chain.
unpack.visual_verb: Colour the incoming axon separately from the receiving neuron.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish proximity from belonging to the same cell.

p007-i37.where_on_page: two circled contact regions in neuron panel
p007-i37.content: synapse — two occurrences identify the contact regions between the previous axon and first neuron, and between the first neuron's axon tips and the next neuron.

teacher_understanding.question: What do the two synapse labels identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: Junction regions at which an incoming axon approaches a receiving neuron.

teacher_understanding.question: Which structures meet near the upper circled synapse?
teacher_understanding.answer: The first neuron's axon tips and the next neuron's receiving branches.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a typical chemical synapse transmit a signal?
teacher_understanding.answer: An arriving impulse causes neurotransmitter release from a terminal; transmitter diffuses across the synaptic cleft and binds receptors on the receiving cell.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should the circled junction not be read as fused cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: At a chemical synapse, the cells remain separated by a small gap; communication occurs through transmitter molecules.

p007-i37.exam_note: Do not claim every synapse is chemical; the chemical mechanism is a standard explanatory example.

terms.plain_meaning: जहाँ एक neuron अगली cell को message देता है
terms.everyday_image: दो लोगों के बीच message देने की छोटी दूरी

why_chain.step: Message एक cell से दूसरी तक जाना चाहिए, लेकिन वे अलग cells हैं।
Typical chemical synapse में transmitter बीच का छोटा gap पार करके signal देता है।

unpack.example_or_place: The two circled junctions in the diagram.
unpack.consequence: Conduction within an axon differs from transmission across a chemical synapse.
unpack.visual_verb: Zoom into the gap and release transmitter dots.
unpack.level_extra: Electrical synapses also exist; avoid making the chemical account universal.

p007-i38.where_on_page: above the left and upper-right neuron bodies
p007-i38.content: neuron cell body — two labels point to the enlarged central regions of the two illustrated neurons.

teacher_understanding.question: What is identified as the neuron cell body?
teacher_understanding.answer: The enlarged central part of each neuron from which the branches extend.

teacher_understanding.question: Which labelled component lies within it?
teacher_understanding.answer: The nucleus lies inside each illustrated cell body.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the cell body support the neuron?
teacher_understanding.answer: It contains the nucleus and much of the machinery for metabolism and protein production, supporting maintenance of the cell and its long processes.

p007-i38.exam_note: Identify cell body separately from dendrites and axon.

terms.plain_meaning: neuron का बड़ा बीच वाला हिस्सा जिसमें nucleus होता है
terms.everyday_image: शाखाओं के बीच मुख्य कामकाजी centre

unpack.example_or_place: Orange central regions in the two neurons.
unpack.consequence: A neuron is more than its long signal-carrying axon.
unpack.visual_verb: Highlight the central region while dimming the processes.
unpack.level_extra: Cell body is also called soma; the book uses neuron cell body.

p007-i39.where_on_page: inside each orange neuron cell body
p007-i39.content: nucleus — two labels point to dark oval structures within the neuron cell bodies.

teacher_understanding.question: What dark structure is labelled in each neuron?
teacher_understanding.answer: The nucleus within the neuron cell body.

teacher_understanding.question: Which region contains these nuclei rather than the long outgoing fiber?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cell body contains the labelled nucleus.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a neuron need a nucleus?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its genetic information supports regulation of cell activity and production of proteins needed to maintain the neuron.

p007-i39.exam_note: Do not confuse the nucleus with an electrical-signal origin symbol.

terms.plain_meaning: cell की genetic जानकारी रखने वाला अंदरूनी हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: मुख्य office का instructions record

unpack.example_or_place: Dark oval inside each neuron body.
unpack.consequence: Neurons remain living cells with ordinary cellular maintenance needs.
unpack.visual_verb: Zoom into each cell body and circle its nucleus.
unpack.level_extra: The action potential is not shown starting from the nucleus.

p007-i40.content: dendrites — leader lines point to the short branching projections around the first neuron's cell body.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the dendrites label point to?
teacher_understanding.answer: Short branched projections extending around the first neuron's cell body.

teacher_understanding.question: Which long process is visually different from these branches?
teacher_understanding.answer: The axon is the long outgoing process connecting towards the next neuron.

teacher_understanding.question: How do dendrites help a neuron receive information?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their branching provides surface for many synaptic inputs, which influence the cell body's electrical state.

p007-i40.exam_note: Typical direction: dendritic input towards the cell body, axonal output away.

terms.plain_meaning: neuron की छोटी शाखाएँ जो incoming messages लेने में मदद करें
terms.everyday_image: कई दिशाओं में फैली पेड़ की डालियाँ

why_chain.step: Neuron को कई दूसरे cells से input मिल सकता है।
फैली dendrites संपर्क के लिए ज्यादा जगह देती हैं।

unpack.example_or_place: Branches around the left neuron.
unpack.consequence: Many inputs can influence one neuron's response.
unpack.visual_verb: Branch outward and receive several incoming signals.
unpack.level_extra: Use typical functional direction without making it an exceptionless rule.

p007-i41.where_on_page: above the curved red fiber connecting the neurons
p007-i41.content: axon — points to the long red process extending from the first neuron towards the next neuron.

teacher_understanding.question: What structure is labelled axon?
teacher_understanding.answer: The long curved process extending from the first cell body towards the second neuron.

teacher_understanding.question: Which direction does the nearby signal arrow indicate?
teacher_understanding.answer: Along that axon towards its far end near the next neuron.

teacher_understanding.question: How does an axon carry an impulse?
teacher_understanding.answer: Successive changes in the axon membrane's electrical state propagate an action potential along the fiber.

p007-i41.exam_note: Axon conducts output towards terminals; do not confuse it with the nucleus or dendrites.

terms.plain_meaning: neuron का लंबा हिस्सा जो impulse आगे ले जाता है
terms.everyday_image: दूर तक message पहुँचाने वाला लंबा रास्ता

unpack.example_or_place: The red curved connection between the illustrated neurons.
unpack.consequence: A neuron can carry information beyond its cell body's immediate neighbourhood.
unpack.visual_verb: Run a moving pulse along the long fiber.
unpack.level_extra: The signal is a membrane event, not a bead physically travelling down a hollow tube.

p007-i42.where_on_page: below the second neuron's receiving region
p007-i42.content: axon tips — points to the terminal branches of the first neuron's axon near the next neuron.

teacher_understanding.question: What do the axon tips represent?
teacher_understanding.answer: The terminal branches at the far end of the first neuron's axon.

teacher_understanding.question: Which neighbouring structures receive their message in the drawing?
teacher_understanding.answer: The dendrites of the next neuron lie next to these tips.

teacher_understanding.question: How do the tips transfer a message at a chemical synapse?
teacher_understanding.answer: An arriving impulse triggers release of neurotransmitter from the terminal into the synaptic cleft.

p007-i42.exam_note: The outgoing neuron's tips and receiving neuron's dendrites belong to different cells.

terms.plain_meaning: axon के आखिरी सिरे जहाँ से अगली cell को signal मिलता है
terms.everyday_image: relay में message सौंपने वाला हाथ

unpack.example_or_place: End of the curved axon beside the upper-right neuron.
unpack.consequence: Conduction along one neuron leads to transmission at its terminal.
unpack.visual_verb: Branch the axon end and release transmitter.
unpack.level_extra: Axon terminals is the standard equivalent term.

p007-i43.content: dendrites of next neuron — points to branching receiving projections of the second neuron.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this receiving-side label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The branches belonging to the next neuron, distinct from the first neuron's axon tips.

teacher_understanding.question: Which neuron owns these branches?
teacher_understanding.answer: The upper-right neuron with its own labelled cell body and nucleus.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a message at these dendrites affect the next neuron?
teacher_understanding.answer: Synaptic input changes the receiving membrane's electrical state; sufficiently combined excitation can lead to a new impulse in that neuron.

p007-i43.exam_note: A received signal does not necessarily cause a new action potential.

terms.plain_meaning: अगले neuron की message लेने वाली शाखाएँ
terms.everyday_image: relay में आगे वाला साथी message लेने को तैयार

unpack.example_or_place: Receiving branches around the upper-right cell body.
unpack.consequence: The input–output pattern can repeat through a chain of neurons.
unpack.visual_verb: Light up the receiving branches, then the next cell body.
unpack.level_extra: Keep the receiving cell distinct from the transmitting cell.

p007-i44.where_on_page: along the curved axon, blue arrow
p007-i44.content: electrical signal — labels the blue directional arrow following the first neuron's axon towards the next neuron.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the blue arrow represent?
teacher_understanding.answer: An electrical signal travelling along the illustrated axon.

teacher_understanding.question: Which direction is shown?
teacher_understanding.answer: From the first neuron's cell-body side towards its axon tips near the next neuron.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a biological electrical signal differ from a household wire current?
teacher_understanding.answer: An action potential is a travelling change in membrane voltage produced by ion movements across the membrane, rather than electrons simply flowing through a metal conductor.

p007-i44.exam_note: Distinguish electrical conduction along the neuron from typical chemical signalling across a synapse.

terms.plain_meaning: membrane के voltage में बदलाव के रूप में आगे बढ़ता message
terms.everyday_image: एक के बाद एक जलती lights से आगे बढ़ती लहर

unpack.example_or_place: The blue arrow beside the curved red axon.
unpack.consequence: The arrow expresses information flow, not the movement of the entire neuron.
unpack.visual_verb: Propagate a brief highlight along successive membrane segments.
unpack.level_extra: Detailed ion-channel phases are unnecessary for this page.

p007-i45.content: Visible sequence: incoming axon of previous neuron → synapse near first neuron → first neuron's cell-body region → long axon carrying electrical signal → axon tips near the next neuron's dendrites and synapse → next neuron's cell-body region.
p007-i45.type_note: Process rather than generic figure: this item explicitly extracts the message-flow sequence represented by the connected structures and arrow.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the message route proceed through the illustrated chain?
teacher_understanding.answer: The incoming connection reaches the first neuron; its long axon carries the indicated electrical signal towards axon tips beside the next neuron's dendrites, where the next synapse occurs.

teacher_understanding.question: When does the axon terminal pass on a typical chemical signal?
teacher_understanding.answer: When an action potential reaches the terminal, it can trigger transmitter release at the synapse.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is receiving a message not identical to generating another impulse?
teacher_understanding.answer: A neuron combines excitatory and inhibitory inputs. A new action potential is generated when conditions at the axon's initiation region reach threshold, so an individual input need not produce an output impulse.

p007-i45.exam_note: Useful sequence question: receiving region → cell body → axon → terminals → next cell.

terms.plain_meaning: message को आगे पहुँचाना
terms.everyday_image: एक साथी से दूसरे तक relay में खबर देना

why_chain.step: एक neuron की पहुँच खत्म होने पर भी message को आगे जाना पड़ सकता है।
Axon terminal अगली cell के साथ synapse बनाकर communication जारी रखता है।

unpack.example_or_place: Follow the page's left-to-upper-right neuron connection.
unpack.consequence: Shows how separate neurons can form an information pathway.
unpack.visual_verb: Animate the route step by step and pause at each synapse.
unpack.level_extra: Teach the typical route without claiming every synaptic input triggers an action potential.

p008-i1.content: Types of Connective Tissues. Columns: Type of Tissue | Location | Function. Rows: Loose connective tissue; Dense connective tissue; Elastic connective tissue; Specialised connective tissue—(i) Cartilage, (ii) Bone, (iii) Vascular connective tissue (blood); Adipose tissue.
p008-i1.type_note: Comparison, rather than the proposed figure: the table compares tissues by location and function.
p008-i1.exam_note: Use the rows for tissue–location–function matching.

p008-i2.type_note: These headers establish the comparison criteria.

p008-i3.content: Type of Tissue: Loose connective tissue | Location: Deep layers of skin, blood vessels, nerves and body organs. | Function: Support and elasticity.
p008-i3.type_note: A location–function comparison row, not merely a figure.

teacher_understanding.question: How does loose connective tissue compare with dense connective tissue in this table?
teacher_understanding.answer: Loose tissue is associated with deep skin layers, blood vessels, nerves and organs, providing support and elasticity; dense tissue is associated with tendons and ligaments and provides great strength.

teacher_understanding.question: Does 'loose' mean that the tissue gives no support?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Its fibres are relatively loosely arranged, allowing packing and flexibility rather than the tightly bundled resistance typical of dense tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is flexible support useful around vessels, nerves and organs?
teacher_understanding.answer: These structures need to remain supported while nearby parts move; a flexible connecting material accommodates movement without making the region rigid.

prerequisites: Tissue as a group of cells and surrounding material
p008-i3.exam_note: Distinguish flexible packing around structures from dense tissue in tendons and ligaments.

terms.plain_meaning: ढीली तरह फैले रेशों वाला tissue, जो आसपास की चीज़ों को सहारा देता है
terms.everyday_image: पैकिंग का नरम भराव सामान को थामता भी है और थोड़ा हिलने भी देता है

terms.plain_meaning: खींचने के बाद पुराने आकार में लौटने की क्षमता
terms.everyday_image: रबर बैंड छोड़ने पर वापस सिकुड़ता है

why_chain.step: Organs, vessels and nerves need support without being fixed rigidly.
Loose connective tissue provides support and elasticity in these regions.

unpack.example_or_place: Think beneath the skin and around the vessels and nerves passing through it.
unpack.consequence: Support need not mean hard or immovable tissue.
unpack.visual_verb: Cushion a vessel with an open fibre mesh.
unpack.level_extra: Use location and function together in matching questions.

p008-i4.content: Type of Tissue: Dense connective tissue | Location: Tendons and ligaments | Function: Compactly pack structures to one another and provides great strength.
p008-i4.type_note: A location–function comparison row, not merely a figure.

teacher_understanding.question: What contrast does the table make between dense and loose connective tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: Dense tissue forms strong connections in tendons and ligaments, whereas loose tissue supports structures such as vessels, nerves and organs with elasticity.

teacher_understanding.question: How do tendons and ligaments differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tendons connect muscle to bone; ligaments connect bone to bone at joints.

teacher_understanding.question: Why do these connections need dense tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Pulling muscles and moving joints place tension on their connections. Closely packed collagen fibres help resist that pulling force.

p008-i4.exam_note: Tendon versus ligament is a useful related distinction; both belong to dense connective tissue.

terms.plain_meaning: पास-पास भरे मज़बूत रेशों वाला जोड़ने का tissue
terms.everyday_image: कई धागे मिलकर मज़बूत रस्सी बनाते हैं

terms.plain_meaning: tendon muscle को bone से, ligament bone को bone से जोड़ता है
terms.everyday_image: हड्डियों के पास खिंचाव सहने वाली मज़बूत पट्टियाँ

why_chain.step: Muscle pull and joint movement can strain connections.
Dense connective tissue supplies strong, compact connections in tendons and ligaments.

unpack.example_or_place: The Achilles tendon behind the ankle is a familiar tendon example.
unpack.consequence: Dense means strong fibrous connection, not mineralised hardness like bone.
unpack.visual_verb: Bundle fibres and pull on the bundle.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid reversing muscle–bone and bone–bone connections.

p008-i5.content: Type of Tissue: Elastic connective tissue | Location: Lungs, arteries, trachea and vocal cords. | Function: Provides elasticity.
p008-i5.type_note: A location–function comparison row, not merely a figure.

teacher_understanding.question: How do the listed roles of elastic and dense connective tissues compare?
teacher_understanding.answer: Elastic tissue provides elasticity in lungs, arteries, trachea and vocal cords; dense tissue provides great strength in tendons and ligaments.

teacher_understanding.question: How does elasticity differ from simply being strong?
teacher_understanding.answer: Elasticity means recovering shape after deformation. Strength concerns resisting damage or breaking under force; the two properties are not identical.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is recoil useful in lungs and arteries?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lungs expand during breathing and arteries stretch as blood is pumped into them. Elastic fibres help these structures return toward their previous dimensions.

prerequisites: Arteries carry blood from the heart
p008-i5.exam_note: Remember the full location set, including trachea and vocal cords.

terms.plain_meaning: खिंचकर फिर पुराने आकार की ओर लौटने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: खींचा हुआ रबर छोड़ते ही लौटता है

terms.plain_meaning: गले में आवाज़ बनाने के लिए कंपन करने वाली तहें
terms.everyday_image: बोलते समय गले के अंदर कंपन

why_chain.step: Breathing and blood pulses repeatedly stretch body structures.
Elastic connective tissue supplies elasticity in the listed structures.

unpack.example_or_place: Follow an inhalation into the lungs and a heartbeat into an artery.
unpack.consequence: Stretch and recoil should be distinguished from rigid support.
unpack.level_extra: A location may contain several tissues; tracheal cartilage and elastic tissue are not contradictory.

p008-i6.where_on_page: specialised connective tissue group, first subrow
p008-i6.content: Type of Tissue: Specialised connective tissue—(i) Cartilage | Location: Ends of long bones, tip of nose, parts of larynx and trachea. | Function: Provides flexibility and support.
p008-i6.type_note: A location–function comparison row, not merely a figure.

teacher_understanding.question: How are cartilage and bone compared on the page?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cartilage provides flexibility and support at long-bone ends, the nose tip and parts of the larynx and trachea. Bone provides protection, support and muscle attachment.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is cartilage not simply another name for bone?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cartilage has a firm but relatively flexible matrix, whereas bone has a mineralised matrix giving much greater rigidity.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is cartilage useful at bone ends and in the airway?
teacher_understanding.answer: At joint surfaces it helps provide smooth, cushioning contact. In parts of the airway it supports the passage while allowing some flexibility.

prerequisites: Matrix as material around tissue cells
p008-i6.exam_note: Match cartilage with flexible support; do not assign bone-like rigidity to it.

terms.plain_meaning: सहारा देने वाला, bone से ज़्यादा लचीला tissue
terms.everyday_image: नाक का सिरा हल्के दबाव पर थोड़ा मुड़ जाता है

terms.plain_meaning: आवाज़ बनने वाला हिस्सा और उससे नीचे हवा जाने की नली
terms.everyday_image: गले से छाती तक जाती साँस की राह

why_chain.step: Some body parts need shape and support without becoming completely rigid.
Cartilage supplies flexibility and support at the listed sites.

unpack.example_or_place: Nose tip; ends of long bones near a joint.
unpack.consequence: Specialised connective tissues include both flexible cartilage and rigid bone.
unpack.visual_verb: Bend the nose tip and cushion bone ends.
unpack.level_extra: The page says parts of the larynx and trachea, not that these organs consist entirely of cartilage.

p008-i7.where_on_page: specialised connective tissue group, second subrow
p008-i7.content: Type of Tissue: Specialised connective tissue—(ii) Bone | Location: Bones | Function: Protection and support muscle attachment.
p008-i7.type_note: A location–function comparison row, not merely a figure.

teacher_understanding.question: Which functions distinguish the bone row from the blood row?
teacher_understanding.answer: Bone provides protection, support and muscle attachment; blood transports oxygen and carbon dioxide and contributes to immune response and clotting.

teacher_understanding.question: How does bone support differ from cartilage support?
teacher_understanding.answer: Bone's mineralised matrix makes it rigid enough for load-bearing and protective frameworks; cartilage provides relatively flexible support.

teacher_understanding.question: How does muscle attachment to bone help movement?
teacher_understanding.answer: A contracting muscle transmits force through its tendon to a bone, moving that bone about a joint.

p008-i7.exam_note: Read the compressed function cell as protection, support and muscle attachment.

terms.plain_meaning: वह जुड़ाव जिससे muscle का खिंचाव bone तक पहुँचता है
terms.everyday_image: डोरी खींचने पर उससे जुड़ा डंडा घूमता है

why_chain.step: The body needs a framework that bears loads and receives muscle pull.
Bone supplies support, protection and attachment for muscles.

unpack.example_or_place: The skull protects the brain; limb bones act as levers.
unpack.consequence: Bone is living connective tissue, not merely a passive hard object.
unpack.visual_verb: Shield an organ and pull a bone lever.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish tissue name 'bone' from the whole organ, which also contains other tissues.

p008-i8.where_on_page: specialised connective tissue group, third subrow
p008-i8.content: Type of Tissue: Specialised connective tissue—(iii) Vascular connective tissue (blood) | Location: Within blood vessels | Function: Transport of oxygen and carbon dioxide and immune response blood clotting.
p008-i8.type_note: A location–function comparison row, not merely a figure.

teacher_understanding.question: How does blood's role differ from the supporting tissues in this table?
teacher_understanding.answer: Blood works within blood vessels in gas transport, immune response and clotting, rather than chiefly providing the mechanical support listed for cartilage and bone.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can fluid blood belong to connective tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Connective tissue need not be solid. Blood has cells suspended in a fluid extracellular matrix, plasma, and links body regions by transport.

teacher_understanding.question: How can blood perform transport, defence and clotting?
teacher_understanding.answer: Red blood cells carry most oxygen, white blood cells participate in defence, and platelets with clotting factors help form clots. Carbon dioxide is transported in several forms, much of it as bicarbonate.

prerequisites: Oxygen use and carbon dioxide production
p008-i8.exam_note: Blood is a specialised connective tissue; do not confuse animal 'vascular' tissue with plant xylem and phloem.

terms.plain_meaning: blood vessels में बहने वाला, चीज़ें एक जगह से दूसरी जगह पहुँचाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: सड़कों पर सामान पहुँचाती गाड़ियाँ

terms.plain_meaning: कीटाणों या दूसरी हानिकारक चीज़ों के खिलाफ शरीर की प्रतिक्रिया
terms.everyday_image: घाव में आए कीटाणों से शरीर की लड़ाई

terms.plain_meaning: चोट पर blood का थक्का बनकर बहाव रोकने में मदद करना
terms.everyday_image: छोटी कटने की जगह पर जमा थक्का

why_chain.step: Distant cells need gas delivery and waste removal, while injuries need defence and sealing.
Blood performs gas transport, immune response and clotting.

unpack.example_or_place: Blood flowing from the lungs to body tissues; a clot after a small cut.
unpack.consequence: Connective tissue classification includes fluid as well as solid tissues.
unpack.visual_verb: Carry gases, intercept germs and seal a cut.
unpack.level_extra: Keep the three listed functions separate in statement-combination questions.

p008-i9.content: Type of Tissue: Adipose tissue | Location: Deep layers of skin, surrounding heart and kidneys and padding around joints. | Function: Support, protection, heat conservation and energy source.
p008-i9.type_note: A location–function comparison row, not merely a figure.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the adipose row compare with loose connective tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Both occur in deep skin layers and provide support. Adipose is additionally listed around the heart, kidneys and joints, with protection, heat conservation and an energy role.

teacher_understanding.question: How do energy storage and heat conservation differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Stored fat can be used as fuel; insulation slows heat loss. These are distinct functions of the same tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is adipose useful beneath skin and around organs?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its fat-rich cells form soft padding that cushions structures, and a subcutaneous layer reduces heat loss while retaining a reserve of chemical energy.

p008-i9.exam_note: Adipose is not just an energy store: protection, support and heat conservation are also listed.

terms.plain_meaning: fat जमा करने वाला tissue, जो नरम padding भी बनाता है
terms.everyday_image: नरम कुशन के साथ रखा हुआ ईंधन

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर की गर्मी जल्दी बाहर न जाने देना
terms.everyday_image: कंबल गर्मी बनने के बजाय गर्मी का निकलना कम करता है

why_chain.step: Organs need cushioning and the body needs to limit heat loss and retain fuel.
Adipose provides protection, support, heat conservation and an energy source.

unpack.example_or_place: Under the skin, around the heart and kidneys, and padding around joints.
unpack.consequence: A single connective tissue can serve mechanical, thermal and energy functions.
unpack.visual_verb: Pad an organ, slow escaping heat and store fat.
unpack.level_extra: Do not reduce adipose function to obesity or energy storage alone.

p008-i10.content: Plant Tissues → Meristematic tissue and Permanent tissue. Meristematic tissue → Apical meristem, Intercalary meristem, Lateral meristem. Permanent tissue → Simple permanent tissue and Complex permanent tissue. Simple permanent tissue → Parenchyma, Collenchyma, Sclerenchyma. Parenchyma → Aerenchyma and Chlorenchyma. Sclerenchyma → Sclerenchyma fibers and Sclereids. Complex permanent tissue → Xylem and Phloem. Connecting lines indicate classification, not a time sequence.
p008-i10.type_note: Classification, rather than the proposed figure: each branch assigns tissue types to a parent group.
prerequisites: Parent and child groups in a classification tree
p008-i10.exam_note: Trace complete parent–child paths; neighbouring labels are not necessarily siblings.

p008-i11.content: Plant Tissues: root group branching to Meristematic tissue and Permanent tissue.
p008-i11.type_note: The label names a classification group.

teacher_understanding.question: Which two groups begin the plant classification?
teacher_understanding.answer: The root divides into meristematic tissue and permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the main distinction behind this division?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meristematic cells actively divide; permanent tissues are differentiated and generally no longer actively dividing.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a plant need both groups?
teacher_understanding.answer: It needs cells that generate growth and differentiated tissues that perform tasks such as support, photosynthesis and transport.

p008-i11.exam_note: Recognise the first-level division before identifying lower branches.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे में मिलकर काम करने वाले cells के समूह
terms.everyday_image: एक पौधे में बढ़ने की जगहें और काम सँभालने वाले हिस्से

why_chain.step: Plants need both continuing growth and specialised work.
The tree separates meristematic and permanent tissue.

unpack.example_or_place: A growing shoot contains both growth regions and mature tissue.
unpack.consequence: All later labels must be traced back to one of these two branches.
unpack.visual_verb: Split the root into two branches.
unpack.level_extra: Do not read classification arrows as transport arrows.

p008-i12.content: Meristematic tissue: child of Plant Tissues; parent of Apical meristem, Intercalary meristem and Lateral meristem.
p008-i12.type_note: The label names a classification group.

teacher_understanding.question: Which meristems belong to this branch?
teacher_understanding.answer: Apical, intercalary and lateral meristems are its three displayed children.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes these three kinds?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are distinguished by position: tips, regions between mature tissues, and sides of stems or roots.

teacher_understanding.question: How does meristematic tissue produce growth?
teacher_understanding.answer: Repeated cell division generates new cells, which can enlarge and differentiate into tissues.

p008-i12.exam_note: These three names classify meristems by position.

terms.plain_meaning: जहाँ cells बार-बार बँटकर नए cells बनाते हैं
terms.everyday_image: पौधे की नई बढ़त बनाने वाली छोटी कार्यशाला

why_chain.step: A growing plant needs a continuing supply of new cells.
Meristematic tissue supplies them through division at growth regions.

unpack.example_or_place: Shoot tips, root tips and other growth regions.
unpack.consequence: Different growth locations produce different kinds of increase in size.
unpack.level_extra: Separate positional classification from the permanent-tissue branches.

p008-i13.content: Apical meristem: child of Meristematic tissue.
p008-i13.type_note: The label identifies a subtype in the classification.

teacher_understanding.question: Which group contains apical meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: It belongs to the meristematic branch, alongside intercalary and lateral meristems.

teacher_understanding.question: How does apical differ from lateral meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Apical meristems occur at root and shoot tips and contribute to length growth; lateral meristems contribute mainly to increased thickness.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is growth at a tip useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: New cells near the advancing tip allow roots and shoots to extend into new soil or above-ground space.

p008-i13.exam_note: Apical means tip; relate position to length growth.

terms.plain_meaning: जड़ या shoot के सिरे पर नए cells बनाने वाला हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: टहनी की बढ़ती नोक

why_chain.step: Roots and shoots need to extend into new space.
Cell production near their tips contributes to length growth.

unpack.example_or_place: A growing shoot tip; root tips are a related standard example.
unpack.consequence: Tip growth is distinct from thickening.
unpack.level_extra: Use apical–tip–length as a linked association.

p008-i14.content: Intercalary meristem: child of Meristematic tissue.
p008-i14.type_note: The label identifies a subtype in the classification.

teacher_understanding.question: Which branch contains intercalary meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is one of the three types under meristematic tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How is its position different from an apical meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: It occurs between differentiated regions, commonly near leaf or internode bases in grasses, rather than at the terminal tip.

teacher_understanding.question: How can this position help grass regrow after cutting?
teacher_understanding.answer: If a basal growth region remains intact, its dividing cells can continue producing growth even after upper portions are removed.

p008-i14.exam_note: Intercalary is not synonymous with lateral; grass regrowth is a useful application.

terms.plain_meaning: बड़े हो चुके हिस्सों के बीच बचा नए cells बनाने वाला क्षेत्र
terms.everyday_image: घास कटने के बाद नीचे बचे हिस्से से फिर बढ़ती है

why_chain.step: Growth can be needed away from the terminal tip.
Intercalary regions allow local elongation between mature tissues.

unpack.example_or_place: Bases of leaves or internodes in grasses.
unpack.consequence: Removing an upper part need not remove every growth region.
unpack.visual_verb: Lengthen a segment from its base.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid the absolute claim that all plants or all nodes have intercalary meristems.

p008-i15.content: Lateral meristem: child of Meristematic tissue.
p008-i15.type_note: The label identifies a subtype in the classification.

teacher_understanding.question: Which larger tissue group includes lateral meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lateral meristem lies under meristematic tissue, not permanent tissue.
