teacher_understanding.answer: It identifies the elongated sclerenchyma form on the left of the right-hand group.

teacher_understanding.question: Which panel is the fibre?
teacher_understanding.answer: The long narrow drawing marked a, rather than the compact stone cell marked b.

teacher_understanding.question: How is a fibre suited to support?
teacher_understanding.answer: Long reinforced cells can form supporting strands, like long threads contributing to a strong cord.

terms.plain_meaning: लंबा और पतला सहारा देने वाला cell
terms.everyday_image: रस्सी में लंबा रेशा

why_chain.step: Long supporting strands benefit from elongated, reinforced cells.

unpack.example_or_place: Sclerenchyma panel a.
unpack.consequence: One tissue category can include differently shaped forms.
unpack.level_extra: The page spells the label 'fiber'.

p010-i20.content: stone cell; b — label points to the compact, irregular thick-walled sclerenchyma form in panel b.

teacher_understanding.question: What is named beside the compact sclerenchyma drawing?
teacher_understanding.answer: The drawing is named a stone cell.

teacher_understanding.question: Which feature distinguishes it from the fibre?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is compact and irregular rather than long and narrow.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is 'stone cell' a useful descriptive name?
teacher_understanding.answer: These thick, lignified cells are hard; clusters of them contribute to the gritty texture of pear pulp. They are also called sclereids.

p010-i20.exam_note: Stone cell/sclereid and pear grittiness are useful standard links.

terms.plain_meaning: पत्थर जैसा सख्त, मोटी दीवार वाला cell
terms.everyday_image: नाशपाती खाते समय महसूस होने वाला किरकिरापन

why_chain.step: Some tissues need local hardness rather than a long strand.
Compact, thick lignified cells provide such hardness.

unpack.example_or_place: Panel b; pear pulp is an outside explanatory example.
unpack.consequence: Sclerenchyma is not restricted to elongated fibres.
unpack.level_extra: Sclereid is the standard alternate name, not printed here.

p010-i21.where_on_page: right group, between fibre and stone cell
p010-i21.content: lumen — leader lines identify the internal cavity enclosed by the thick walls.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the lumen?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is the cavity inside the cell wall, rather than a gap between two cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which part of the drawings does this label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: It identifies the internal space of the sclerenchyma forms.

teacher_understanding.question: How does wall thickening affect the lumen?
teacher_understanding.answer: Wall material deposited towards the interior leaves a narrower internal cavity.

terms.plain_meaning: दीवार से घिरी अंदर की जगह
terms.everyday_image: मोटी नली के बीच का खाली रास्ता

why_chain.step: To understand a thick wall, separate the wall material from the cavity it encloses.

unpack.example_or_place: Sclerenchyma drawings.
unpack.consequence: The central cavity is not an intercellular gap.

p010-i22.content: Sclerenchyma Tissue — caption names the right-hand fibre and stone-cell group.

teacher_understanding.question: What tissue category unites the fibre and stone cell?
teacher_understanding.answer: The figure groups both under Sclerenchyma Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which labelled feature connects the two forms?
teacher_understanding.answer: Both are associated with cell walls containing lignin.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this caption extend the page's classification?
teacher_understanding.answer: It supplies the third simple permanent tissue name visually, beyond the two detailed text sections on this page.

p010-i22.exam_note: Completes the three named simple tissues.

why_chain.step: Group the two different shapes by their shared reinforced-wall tissue identity.

unpack.example_or_place: Right-hand group.
unpack.consequence: Previews the next tissue section without inventing its text.
unpack.level_extra: Parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma are the three names to distinguish.

p010-i24.content: Occurrence: In leaf stalks and stems of dicots.

teacher_understanding.question: Which locations are specified for collenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Leaf stalks and stems of dicots are the stated locations.

teacher_understanding.question: What qualification must be retained in the stem location?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page says stems 'of dicots', not stems without qualification.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is flexible support useful in these places?
teacher_understanding.answer: A leaf stalk carries a leaf that moves in wind, and growing stems must withstand bending while continuing to extend.

p010-i24.exam_note: Location matching; retain the dicot qualification.

terms.plain_meaning: पत्ते को तने से जोड़ने वाला डंठल
terms.everyday_image: पत्ता पकड़ने का छोटा डंठल

terms.plain_meaning: ऐसे flowering plants जिनके seed में दो seed leaves होते हैं
terms.everyday_image: भीगे चने के दो हिस्से

why_chain.step: Leaf stalks and young stems need support without becoming completely rigid.
Collenchyma supplies flexible support in such locations.

unpack.example_or_place: Trace from a familiar leaf blade along its stalk into the stem.
unpack.consequence: Connects location to the bending function below.
unpack.level_extra: Petiole is the standard name for a leaf stalk.

p010-i26.content:
• Living
• Elongated
• Irregularly thickened at corners.
• Very little intercellular space.

teacher_understanding.question: What four features characterise collenchyma cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are living and elongated, with irregular corner thickening and very little intercellular space.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is the thickening concentrated?
teacher_understanding.answer: At cell corners, rather than being described as uniformly distributed around the wall.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these features support flexible growth?
teacher_understanding.answer: Closely packed elongated living cells provide continuity, while unevenly thickened primary walls reinforce the tissue without the rigidity of strongly lignified walls.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this differ from the stated parenchyma structure?
teacher_understanding.answer: Parenchyma is described as thin-walled with intercellular spaces; collenchyma has corner thickening and very little space. Elongation by itself does not distinguish them because parenchyma may also be elongated.

p010-i26.exam_note: High-value combination: living + elongated + uneven corner thickening + little space.

terms.plain_meaning: काम करते समय cell का जिंदा रहना
terms.everyday_image: सिर्फ खाली खोल नहीं, अंदर काम चलता रहना

terms.plain_meaning: दीवार का कोनों पर ज्यादा मोटा होना, हर जगह बराबर नहीं
terms.everyday_image: बैग के कोनों पर लगा अतिरिक्त मजबूत कपड़ा

terms.plain_meaning: cells का पास-पास होना, बीच में बहुत कम जगह
terms.everyday_image: सटाकर रखे डिब्बे

why_chain.step: Growing plant parts need reinforcement without losing their ability to bend.
Living elongated cells with uneven wall reinforcement provide flexible support.

unpack.example_or_place: Leaf stalks and dicot stems; compare the middle diagram.
unpack.consequence: Wall distribution and packing explain the next function list.
unpack.level_extra: Very little space is not the same wording as no space; thickened does not automatically mean dead.

p010-i28.content:
➢ Provides mechanical strength
➢ Provides flexibility and photosynthesis
➢ Allowed bending of parts.
p010-i28.type_note: These are functional outcomes of collenchyma, including bending, not a description of spatial parts.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are strength and flexibility listed together?
teacher_understanding.answer: Plant parts need support against forces but also need to bend rather than snap; collenchyma supplies this combination.

teacher_understanding.question: How does its cell structure enable these outcomes?
teacher_understanding.answer: Unevenly thickened, non-rigid primary walls reinforce living cells while permitting some extension and bending.

teacher_understanding.question: Which functions does the page explicitly assign to collenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mechanical strength, flexibility, photosynthesis and bending of parts are listed.

teacher_understanding.question: What condition is needed for its stated photosynthesis function?
teacher_understanding.answer: Collenchyma cells can photosynthesise when they contain chloroplasts; mechanical support does not itself imply photosynthesis.

p010-i28.exam_note: Flexible support is the central association; do not universalise photosynthesis.

terms.plain_meaning: खींचने या दबाव पड़ने पर सहारा बनाए रखने की ताकत
terms.everyday_image: वजन सँभालता मजबूत डंडा

terms.plain_meaning: बिना टूटे मुड़ पाने की क्षमता
terms.everyday_image: हवा में झुकती नरम टहनी

why_chain.step: Wind and movement bend stalks, so support must not make them brittle.
Collenchyma combines mechanical strength with flexibility and allows bending.

unpack.example_or_place: A leaf stalk bending as its leaf moves in wind.
unpack.consequence: Explains why flexible plant parts are the examples that follow.
unpack.level_extra: Contrast flexible collenchyma support with lignified sclerenchyma support; this mechanism is standard explanation.

p010-i29.content: E.g. Tendrils and stems of climbers

teacher_understanding.question: Which examples illustrate flexible support?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page gives tendrils and stems of climbers.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are climbing parts helpful examples?
teacher_understanding.answer: They must bend around or follow supports while remaining strong enough to retain their form.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the tendril example be connected to the function without overstating it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Collenchyma helps a growing part withstand bending. Tendril coiling itself involves a growth response to contact; the tissue should not be described as independently causing that response.

p010-i29.exam_note: Example–tissue matching; distinguish support from the mechanism of coiling.

terms.plain_meaning: पतले हिस्से जो सहारे के चारों ओर लिपट सकते हैं
terms.everyday_image: जाली से लिपटा मटर का tendril

terms.plain_meaning: सहारा पकड़कर ऊपर बढ़ने वाले पौधे
terms.everyday_image: डंडे या जाली पर चढ़ती बेल

why_chain.step: A climbing plant needs parts that can bend around support without easily breaking.
The page uses tendrils and climber stems to illustrate flexible support.

unpack.example_or_place: Tendrils and stems of climbers; a pea tendril is a standard everyday illustration.
unpack.consequence: Closes the link from cell-wall arrangement to a visible plant function.
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer that every part of a climber consists only of collenchyma.

p011-i2.content:
Occurrence:
• In stems around vascular bundles.
• In veins of leaves.
• Hard covering of seeds and nuts.

teacher_understanding.question: What distribution of sclerenchyma does the page describe?
teacher_understanding.answer: It occurs around stem vascular bundles, in leaf veins and in the hard coverings of seeds and nuts.

teacher_understanding.question: Where should a learner look for the stem and leaf examples?
teacher_understanding.answer: Look around the conducting bundles inside a stem and along the vein framework of a leaf.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is strengthening tissue useful at these sites?
teacher_understanding.answer: Stems and leaf veins need resistance to bending, while seed and nut coverings need resistance to physical damage.

prerequisites: vascular bundle as a group of conducting tissues

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे में पानी और भोजन ले जाने वाले tissues के गुच्छे
terms.everyday_image: एक साथ बँधी पानी की पाइपें

why_chain.step: Stems, veins and coverings face bending or physical damage.
Sclerenchyma provides mechanical strength and protection at such sites.

unpack.example_or_place: Trace a familiar leaf's veins, then zoom into supporting tissue.
unpack.consequence: Location can help identify the tissue's support role.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish tissue around vascular bundles from the conducting bundle itself.

teacher_understanding.question: What familiar example identifies sclerenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page gives coconut husk as its example.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is the husk on a coconut?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is the fibrous outer covering outside the hard shell.

teacher_understanding.question: How does handling coconut husk help explain this tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its tough fibres resist pulling apart, giving an everyday experience of mechanical strength.

p011-i3.exam_note: Classic tissue–example match; distinguish husk from shell.

terms.plain_meaning: नारियल के बाहर का रेशेदार हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: नारियल से खींचकर अलग किए जाने वाले भूरे रेशे

why_chain.step: A coconut needs a protective outer covering.
Tough sclerenchyma fibres provide a familiar example of protective strength.

unpack.example_or_place: Coconut husk.
unpack.consequence: A daily-life object anchors sclerenchyma identification.
unpack.level_extra: Remember the printed example precisely.

p011-i4.content:
Structure:
➢ Long and narrow
➢ Walls are thickened by LIGNINS

teacher_understanding.question: What shape and wall property does the book assign to sclerenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cells are described as long and narrow, with walls thickened by lignins.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is the strengthening material deposited?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lignin is deposited in the cell wall rather than being a filling between neighbouring cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does lignification help support?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lignin makes walls rigid and resistant to deformation, allowing them to bear mechanical stress.

teacher_understanding.question: Does the long-and-narrow description cover all sclerenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: It particularly describes fibres. Sclereids are another sclerenchyma form and can have other shapes.

p011-i4.exam_note: Lignified wall is a key identifying feature; avoid generalising fibre shape to all forms.

terms.plain_meaning: लंबाई ज़्यादा, चौड़ाई कम
terms.everyday_image: पतली लंबी डोरी

terms.plain_meaning: cell wall को कड़ा बनाने वाला substance
terms.everyday_image: दीवार को मज़बूत करने वाला अतिरिक्त भराव

why_chain.step: A plant needs walls that resist bending and compression.
Lignin reinforces those walls, producing rigid support.

unpack.example_or_place: Coconut husk fibres.
unpack.consequence: Thick walls explain strength better than memorising the tissue name alone.
unpack.level_extra: Know lignin as the wall-strengthening material; recognise the fibre-shape qualification.

p011-i5.content: ➢ Cell cavity is absent due to excessive thickness.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the page say the cell cavity is absent?
teacher_understanding.answer: It attributes the absence to excessive wall thickness.

teacher_understanding.question: How should this be understood accurately?
teacher_understanding.answer: Wall deposition reduces the internal space, called the lumen. In sclerenchyma the lumen is commonly narrow, not necessarily completely absent.

p011-i5.exam_note: Distinguish thick wall and reduced lumen from a universal absence of lumen.

terms.plain_meaning: cell wall के भीतर की जगह
terms.everyday_image: मोटी दीवार वाले पाइप का छोटा अंदरूनी रास्ता

why_chain.step: Support requires a strongly reinforced wall.
Increasing wall thickness reduces the internal cavity; complete absence is not universal.

unpack.example_or_place: A cross-section through a sclerenchyma fibre.
unpack.consequence: Keep the inside-cell lumen distinct from spaces between cells.
unpack.level_extra: The printed absolute is qualified rather than silently adopted.

p011-i6.content:
➢ Intercellular spaces absent.
➢ Cells are dead.

teacher_understanding.question: What arrangement and living status are stated?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page describes cells without intercellular spaces and identifies the cells as dead.

teacher_understanding.question: Where would an intercellular space be, unlike a cell cavity?
teacher_understanding.answer: It would lie between neighbouring cells; a cell cavity lies inside one cell's wall.

teacher_understanding.question: How can dead cells still provide support?
teacher_understanding.answer: At maturity, the protoplasm is lost but the thick walls remain, so physical reinforcement does not require a living cell interior.

p011-i6.exam_note: Dead at maturity versus living support tissues is a common comparison.

terms.plain_meaning: पास-पास के cells के बीच की खाली जगह
terms.everyday_image: जुड़ी ईंटों के बीच बचा गैप

why_chain.step: A support framework must remain mechanically firm.
Closely arranged thick walls can provide support after the living contents are lost.

unpack.example_or_place: Mature sclerenchyma.
unpack.consequence: Dead does not mean functionless.
unpack.level_extra: Separate cell cavity, intercellular space and living status in statement questions.

p011-i7.content:
Function:
• Provide strength to plant cell.
• Provides protection and mechanical strength

teacher_understanding.question: Why is sclerenchyma useful to a plant?
teacher_understanding.answer: It provides strength, protection and mechanical strength.

teacher_understanding.question: How do its structural features produce these benefits?
teacher_understanding.answer: Rigid lignified walls form a reinforcing framework that resists deformation and helps protect enclosed parts.

p011-i7.exam_note: Match structure with function; do not confuse support with food transport.

terms.plain_meaning: दबाव, खिंचाव या मुड़ने पर टूटने से बचने की ताकत
terms.everyday_image: इमारत का मज़बूत ढाँचा

why_chain.step: Plant parts experience forces that could bend or damage them.
Sclerenchyma supplies a rigid protective framework.

unpack.example_or_place: Hard seed coverings and coconut husk.
unpack.consequence: Location, thick walls and protective function form one explanation.
unpack.level_extra: Use a location–structure–function chain for correct-statement questions.

p011-i9.content:
• Made up of more than one type of cells.
• Cells co-ordinate to perform common function.

teacher_understanding.question: What makes this tissue complex?
teacher_understanding.answer: Different cell types form one tissue and coordinate for a common function.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is this organisation illustrated on the page?
teacher_understanding.answer: The xylem and phloem drawings show several labelled components within each tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can several cell types be useful in one tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: A transport system needs conducting routes as well as support and associated living cells, so different cells can divide the work.

p011-i9.exam_note: Complex means multiple cell types, not merely a large number of cells.

terms.plain_meaning: अलग-अलग काम करके एक साझा काम पूरा करना
terms.everyday_image: रसोई में कोई काटता है, कोई पकाता है, खाना मिलकर बनता है

why_chain.step: Transport needs more than an unsupported passage.
Different cell types work together as a complex tissue.

unpack.example_or_place: Xylem combines conducting cells, parenchyma and fibres.
unpack.consequence: This prepares the learner to recognise components rather than treat xylem as one cell.
unpack.level_extra: Contrast with simple permanent tissue using cell-type diversity as the criterion.

p011-i10.content:
Functions:
• Transport water, minerals and food materials.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a plant need transport tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Water and minerals are obtained mainly through roots, whereas food is made mainly in leaves; other parts need supplies from these sources.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the page describe the contribution of complex tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: They transport water, minerals and food materials.

teacher_understanding.question: How is this transport divided between the two named tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem mainly transports water and minerals; phloem transports food substances.

p011-i10.exam_note: Do not assign all three transported materials equally to each tissue.

terms.plain_meaning: ज़रूरी चीज़ों को एक हिस्से से दूसरे तक पहुँचाना
terms.everyday_image: घर में टंकी से अलग-अलग नलों तक पानी पहुँचना

why_chain.step: Places of supply and places of use are separated in a plant.
Complex tissues move water, minerals and food between plant parts.

unpack.example_or_place: Roots, stem and leaves linked by conducting tissues.
unpack.consequence: Different transport roles lead to xylem–phloem comparison.
unpack.level_extra: Know the cargo associated with each tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which two complex permanent tissues are named?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem and phloem are the two types listed.

teacher_understanding.question: What main functional difference separates them?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem mainly conducts water and minerals, while phloem carries food substances.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are both still in the same broad group?
teacher_understanding.answer: Each contains different cell types coordinating in transport, which is the basis of complex-tissue organisation.

p011-i11.exam_note: Classify xylem and phloem as complex permanent tissues.

terms.plain_meaning: मुख्यतः पानी और minerals पहुँचाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: पानी पहुँचाने वाली पाइप-व्यवस्था

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे में बना भोजन पहुँचाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: तैयार खाना अलग-अलग जगह पहुँचाने वाली व्यवस्था

why_chain.step: Plants need water supplies and distribution of food.
Xylem and phloem specialise in these different transport roles.

unpack.example_or_place: The paired diagrams on this page.
unpack.consequence: Both are complex tissues but are not interchangeable.
unpack.level_extra: Use the hierarchy: permanent tissue → complex → xylem/phloem.

p011-i12.content: Complex Permanent Tissue: paired labelled drawings of Xylem and Phloem. Xylem shows elongated conducting and supporting elements with surrounding parenchyma. Phloem shows stacked sieve-tube regions, adjacent companion cells, fibres and parenchyma. Leader arrows identify parts; they do not indicate transport direction.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the paired figure demonstrate?
teacher_understanding.answer: Each named complex tissue consists of several different components, not one uniform cell type.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissues are shown side by side?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem is on the left and phloem on the right.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the arrows be read?
teacher_understanding.answer: Follow each leader from a component to its name; these are identification arrows rather than a diagram of flow.

why_chain.step: A complex tissue must contain different cell types.
The labels reveal the different parts within each tissue.

unpack.example_or_place: Paired vascular-tissue illustration.
unpack.consequence: A component must be matched to the correct tissue.
unpack.level_extra: Do not interpret leader arrows as movement arrows.

p011-i13.content: Xylem Parenchyma — leader identifies parenchyma in the xylem drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The parenchyma component of xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which functions does the page attach to it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Food storage and sideways conduction of water.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this expand the idea of a water-conducting tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem includes storage and lateral-transfer cells alongside the main conducting elements.

p011-i13.exam_note: A xylem component with storage and lateral-conduction roles.

terms.plain_meaning: xylem में भोजन जमा करने और पानी बगल में पहुँचाने वाले cells
terms.everyday_image: मुख्य पाइप के पास छोटा भंडार और बगल का रास्ता

unpack.example_or_place: Xylem drawing.
unpack.consequence: Xylem is more than hollow conduits.
unpack.level_extra: Connect label to storage and sideways conduction.

p011-i14.content: Vessels — leader identifies the broad conducting element in xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: What is labelled Vessels?
teacher_understanding.answer: A conducting component of the xylem drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: Which other component shares its conducting role?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tracheids also transport water and minerals.

teacher_understanding.question: How is the vessel suited to conduction?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its tubular structure provides a route for vertical water and mineral transport.

p011-i14.exam_note: Plant vessels here are not blood vessels.

terms.plain_meaning: xylem के पानी ले जाने वाले नली जैसे हिस्से
terms.everyday_image: जुड़े पाइपों का रास्ता

unpack.example_or_place: Broad element in the xylem figure.
unpack.consequence: Links tube shape to transport.
unpack.level_extra: Match vessels with xylem.

p011-i15.content: Tracheids — leader identifies the elongated conducting elements of xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does Tracheids name?
teacher_understanding.answer: One of the four components listed for xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which transport role is associated with them?
teacher_understanding.answer: They conduct water and minerals vertically, together with vessels.

teacher_understanding.question: How does their shape support the role?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their elongated tubular form supplies a route along the plant.

p011-i15.exam_note: Tracheids belong to xylem, not phloem.

terms.plain_meaning: पानी और minerals ले जाने वाले लंबे xylem cells
terms.everyday_image: लंबी पतली नलियों की कतार

unpack.example_or_place: Elongated xylem elements.
unpack.consequence: Two kinds of conducting elements must be recognised.
unpack.level_extra: Pair tracheids with vessels for conduction.

p011-i16.content: Xylem Fibres — leader identifies the supporting fibres in xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The fibre component within xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which principal function belongs to these fibres?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their function is mainly supportive.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are fibres useful beside conduits?
teacher_understanding.answer: They reinforce the tissue and help it resist mechanical forces.

p011-i16.exam_note: Do not assign the main conducting role to xylem fibres.

terms.plain_meaning: xylem को सहारा देने वाले लंबे मज़बूत cells
terms.everyday_image: पाइप के साथ लगा सहारा

unpack.example_or_place: Xylem illustration.
unpack.consequence: Support is part of complex-tissue teamwork.
unpack.level_extra: Support versus conduction is the key distinction.

p011-i17.content: Phloem Parenchyma — leader identifies parenchyma in the phloem drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: What component is named?
teacher_understanding.answer: Parenchyma belonging to phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which complex tissue contains this labelled component?
teacher_understanding.answer: The right-hand tissue, phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does phloem parenchyma contribute?
teacher_understanding.answer: These living cells help store food and participate in lateral movement of food substances.

p011-i17.exam_note: Parenchyma occurs in both named complex tissues.

terms.plain_meaning: phloem में भोजन सँभालने वाले living cells
terms.everyday_image: डिलीवरी रास्ते के पास छोटा भंडार

unpack.example_or_place: Right-hand phloem diagram.
unpack.consequence: The word parenchyma alone does not identify xylem exclusively.
unpack.level_extra: Use the xylem/phloem qualifier.

p011-i18.content: Companion cell — leader identifies the slender cell beside a sieve tube.

teacher_understanding.question: What is labelled beside the sieve tube?
teacher_understanding.answer: A companion cell in phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue should be associated with companion cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem, as shown in the right-hand illustration.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this neighbouring cell important?
teacher_understanding.answer: It supports sieve-tube function through close metabolic cooperation and helps in loading and unloading sugars.

p011-i18.exam_note: Companion cell is a diagnostic phloem label.

terms.plain_meaning: sieve tube के पास रहकर उसका काम सँभालने वाला cell
terms.everyday_image: मुख्य काम करने वाले के पास उसका सहायक

unpack.example_or_place: Beside the sieve tube in phloem.
unpack.consequence: Transport cells work with neighbouring cells.
unpack.level_extra: Recognise the sieve tube–companion cell association.

p011-i19.content: Phloem fibres — leader identifies the elongated supporting component in phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: What part does this label name?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fibres within the phloem tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which other illustrated tissue also contains fibres?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem also has labelled fibres.

teacher_understanding.question: How do phloem fibres contribute?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their thick walls provide mechanical support rather than acting as the main food-conducting route.

p011-i19.exam_note: Fibres are not exclusive to xylem.

terms.plain_meaning: phloem को मज़बूती देने वाले रेशे जैसे cells
terms.everyday_image: नली के साथ बँधी मज़बूत डोरी

unpack.example_or_place: Phloem drawing.
unpack.consequence: Supporting cells coexist with food-conducting cells.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish fibres from sieve tubes.

p011-i20.content: Sieve tube — leader identifies the main elongated tube in phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: What main phloem structure is labelled?
teacher_understanding.answer: The sieve tube.

teacher_understanding.question: Which neighbouring cell is also labelled?
teacher_understanding.answer: A companion cell lies beside it.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a sieve tube serve transport?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sieve-tube elements join end to end, with perforated end regions allowing movement of food-containing sap.

p011-i20.exam_note: Sieve tube belongs to phloem, unlike vessels and tracheids.

terms.plain_meaning: भोजन वाला रस ले जाने वाली phloem की नली
terms.everyday_image: बीच-बीच में छन्नी जैसे जोड़ वाला पाइप

unpack.example_or_place: Large phloem tube in the right illustration.
unpack.consequence: The lower figure explains its component cells and end plates.
unpack.level_extra: Match sieve tube with food transport.

p011-i21.content: Xylem structure / Phloem structure. The xylem side shows an isolated vessel element with pitted walls (a), tracheids, and a grouped view (b) labelled xylem parenchyma cell, vessel element, pitted walls and tracheid. The phloem side shows an isolated sieve-tube element with sieve plate, companion cell, nucleus and phloem parenchyma cells, alongside a grouped view (b) labelled companion cell, sieve-tube element, sieve plate, phloem parenchyma cells and plasmo-desmata [plasmodesmata]. Leader lines identify structures rather than flow directions.

teacher_understanding.question: What extra detail does the boxed figure add?
teacher_understanding.answer: It shows individual elements and grouped arrangements, including pitted xylem walls and the sieve plates and associated cells of phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which parts connect the figure to transport pathways?
teacher_understanding.answer: Vessel elements and tracheids are shown on the xylem side; sieve-tube elements and sieve plates on the phloem side.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these details improve understanding beyond a tissue name?
teacher_understanding.answer: They distinguish the tube-forming cells from the neighbouring support and storage cells, and show specialised regions through which exchange or continuity occurs.

p011-i21.exam_note: Recognise pits versus sieve plates and individual elements versus whole tubes.

why_chain.step: A transport route needs continuity along its length and connections with nearby cells.
The detailed views reveal wall pits, sieve plates and cell connections.

unpack.example_or_place: Boxed lower illustration.
unpack.consequence: Transport tissue is an organised assembly, not a featureless pipe.
unpack.level_extra: Panel letters a and b mark views, not biological structures.

p011-i22.where_on_page: boxed figure, far-left isolated xylem cell
p011-i22.content: vessel elements — leader points to the isolated elongated pink vessel element.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the isolated pink structure?
teacher_understanding.answer: A vessel element, identified by the label vessel elements.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue contains it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does an element differ from the whole vessel?
teacher_understanding.answer: An element is one constituent cell; vessel elements connect end to end to form a vessel.

terms.plain_meaning: मिलकर vessel बनाने वाले अलग-अलग cells
terms.everyday_image: लंबी पाइप बनाने वाले छोटे पाइप के टुकड़े

unpack.example_or_place: Far-left pink cell.
unpack.consequence: One cell need not equal the entire conduit.
unpack.level_extra: Read element as a building unit.

p011-i23.where_on_page: boxed figure, beside isolated vessel element
p011-i23.content: pitted walls — leader points to pits in the isolated vessel element's wall.

teacher_understanding.question: What wall feature is labelled?
teacher_understanding.answer: Pitted walls on the isolated vessel element.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue's conducting element shows these pits?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How do pits help conduction?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are regions where secondary wall thickening is absent, facilitating water movement between adjacent cells through the remaining pit membranes.

p011-i23.exam_note: Pits are wall regions, not sieve plates.

terms.plain_meaning: मोटी wall में कम मोटाई वाले छोटे-छोटे हिस्से
terms.everyday_image: मोटी दीवार में पतली खिड़की जैसी जगहें

unpack.example_or_place: Isolated xylem vessel element.
unpack.consequence: A thick wall can still allow lateral exchange.
unpack.level_extra: Do not imagine every pit as a completely empty hole.

p011-i24.content: tracheids — leader points to the narrow, tapered pink cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What cells are labelled tracheids?
teacher_understanding.answer: The elongated tapered cells shown between the isolated vessel and grouped xylem view.

teacher_understanding.question: Which listed tissue component do they represent?
teacher_understanding.answer: The tracheid component of xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does water move between adjoining tracheids?
teacher_understanding.answer: It passes through pit regions in their overlapping walls.

terms.plain_meaning: सिरों पर पतले होते लंबे पानी ले जाने वाले cells
terms.everyday_image: पास-पास रखी नुकीले सिरों वाली पतली नलियाँ

unpack.example_or_place: Narrow pink cells in the boxed xylem figure.
unpack.consequence: Their form differs from broad vessel elements.
unpack.level_extra: Use shape alongside the label, not colour alone.

p011-i25.where_on_page: boxed figure, top of grouped xylem
p011-i25.content: xylem parenchyma cell — leader points to the slender grey cell beside the pink vessel elements.

teacher_understanding.question: What is identified beside the vessel?
teacher_understanding.answer: A xylem parenchyma cell.

teacher_understanding.question: Which page functions belong to this cell type?
teacher_understanding.answer: Food storage and sideways water conduction.

teacher_understanding.question: Why show it beside conducting elements?
teacher_understanding.answer: That arrangement illustrates how lateral-transfer and storage cells belong to the same complex tissue as the main conduits.

unpack.example_or_place: Grey cell beside grouped pink xylem elements.
unpack.consequence: Connects the diagram with the storage and lateral-conduction statement.
unpack.level_extra: Do not call every elongated xylem cell a vessel.

p011-i26.content: vessel element — leader points to a broad pink element in the grouped xylem view.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this second vessel label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: A vessel element within the grouped xylem view rather than the isolated view.

teacher_understanding.question: Which function links this to tracheids?
teacher_understanding.answer: Both conduct water and minerals vertically.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the grouped view improve on the isolated view?
teacher_understanding.answer: It places the conducting element alongside other cell types, making the organisation of complex tissue visible.

p011-i26.exam_note: Same component shown in a different view.

unpack.example_or_place: Broad pink element in grouped xylem.
unpack.consequence: An isolated cell and a tissue view can depict the same component.
unpack.level_extra: Recognise the part across views.

p011-i27.where_on_page: boxed figure, left of grouped xylem
p011-i27.content: pitted walls — leader points to wall pits in the grouped xylem elements.

teacher_understanding.question: What feature is repeated in the grouped view?
teacher_understanding.answer: Pitted walls of the xylem elements.

teacher_understanding.question: Which isolated element also has this label?
teacher_understanding.answer: The isolated vessel element at the far left.

teacher_understanding.question: How can pits reconcile strength with exchange?
teacher_understanding.answer: Most of the secondary wall is reinforced, while pit regions permit water exchange through thinner wall regions.

p011-i27.exam_note: Repeated structural detail, not a new cell type.

unpack.example_or_place: Grouped xylem wall markings.
unpack.consequence: Wall reinforcement need not eliminate cell-to-cell transfer.
unpack.level_extra: Separate a wall feature from a tissue component.

p011-i28.content: tracheid — small label beneath the grouped xylem drawing; a clear leader line is not visible.

teacher_understanding.question: What component is named below the grouped drawing?
teacher_understanding.answer: A tracheid.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue does it belong to?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How should this label be used despite the unclear pointer?
teacher_understanding.answer: Use it to identify the named xylem component, but do not infer a precise pointed cell from the unclear leader.

p011-i28.exam_note: Biological identification is clear; exact pointer is not.

unpack.example_or_place: Base of grouped xylem illustration.
unpack.consequence: Preserves the label without inventing visual precision.
unpack.level_extra: Use the clearer isolated tracheid view to learn its shape.

p011-i29.content: sieve plate — leader points to the end region of the isolated sieve-tube element.

teacher_understanding.question: What end structure is labelled?
teacher_understanding.answer: A sieve plate on the sieve-tube element.

teacher_understanding.question: Which conducting tissue has this structure?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a sieve plate permit continuity?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its pores allow sap to move between adjoining sieve-tube elements.

p011-i29.exam_note: Sieve plate versus xylem wall pits.

terms.plain_meaning: छोटे छेदों वाला जोड़, जिससे sieve-tube elements के बीच रस जा सके
terms.everyday_image: दो हिस्सों के बीच छन्नी जैसी प्लेट

unpack.example_or_place: Top of isolated blue sieve-tube element.
unpack.consequence: Separate cells can form a continuous transport route.
unpack.level_extra: Plate is a structure, not a separate cell type.

p011-i30.where_on_page: boxed figure, isolated phloem left label
p011-i30.content: sieve-tube element — leader points to the long blue conducting cell.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the long blue cell represent?
teacher_understanding.answer: A sieve-tube element.

teacher_understanding.question: Which larger structure is formed from such elements?
teacher_understanding.answer: A sieve tube in phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How are successive elements linked?
teacher_understanding.answer: They meet end to end at sieve plates, permitting movement of sap.

p011-i30.exam_note: Distinguish an element from a complete sieve tube.

terms.plain_meaning: sieve tube बनाने वाला एक लंबा cell
terms.everyday_image: लंबी नली का एक खंड

unpack.example_or_place: Isolated blue phloem cell.
unpack.consequence: Clarifies cell versus tissue-level transport route.
unpack.level_extra: Element means one unit.

p011-i31.where_on_page: boxed figure, beside isolated phloem cell
p011-i31.content: companion cell — leader points to the smaller cell alongside the isolated sieve-tube element.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the smaller neighbouring cell?
teacher_understanding.answer: A companion cell.

teacher_understanding.question: Which cell is it shown accompanying?
teacher_understanding.answer: The sieve-tube element.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does close association matter?
teacher_understanding.answer: Companion cells help maintain the activity of sieve-tube elements and assist sugar transfer.

unpack.example_or_place: Beside the isolated blue sieve-tube element.
unpack.consequence: Shows cooperation at the cell level.
unpack.level_extra: Companion cell is not a sieve plate.

p011-i32.where_on_page: boxed figure, right of isolated phloem view
p011-i32.content: nucleus — leader points to the dark body in the companion cell next to the sieve-tube element.

teacher_understanding.question: What small internal structure is labelled?
teacher_understanding.answer: A nucleus in the companion-cell region of the illustration.

teacher_understanding.question: Which cell retains a nucleus in the mature sieve-tube–companion-cell pair?
teacher_understanding.answer: The companion cell retains a nucleus; the mature sieve-tube element lacks one.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this help explain their cooperation?
teacher_understanding.answer: The nucleated companion cell supports the metabolic needs of the associated sieve-tube element.

p011-i32.exam_note: Living but non-nucleated mature sieve-tube elements are an important exception.

terms.plain_meaning: cell के काम का नियंत्रण और आनुवंशिक जानकारी रखने वाला हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: काम सँभालने वाला नियंत्रण कक्ष

unpack.example_or_place: Companion cell in the isolated phloem view.
unpack.consequence: Absence of nucleus does not by itself mean a mature sieve-tube element is dead.
unpack.level_extra: Keep mature sieve tubes distinct from dead mature xylem conduits.

p011-i33.where_on_page: boxed figure, left of isolated phloem lower region
p011-i33.content: phloem parenchyma cells — label identifies associated parenchyma in the isolated phloem view.

teacher_understanding.question: What additional cells are identified here?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem parenchyma cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue includes them?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How are they different from sieve-tube elements in role?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are associated living storage and lateral-transfer cells rather than the main longitudinal food-conducting elements.

unpack.example_or_place: Associated cells in the isolated phloem view.
unpack.consequence: Not every phloem cell forms the conducting tube.
unpack.level_extra: Parenchyma and companion cells are different labels.

p011-i34.content: companion cell — leader points to the narrow cell beside the grouped sieve-tube elements.

teacher_understanding.question: What is labelled at the top of the grouped phloem view?
teacher_understanding.answer: A companion cell beside the sieve-tube elements.

teacher_understanding.question: Which earlier view shows the same association?
teacher_understanding.answer: The isolated phloem view immediately to its left.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the grouped view show organisation?
teacher_understanding.answer: It locates the companion cell alongside the tube rather than as part of the sieve plate.

p011-i34.exam_note: Recognise the same component in grouped and isolated views.

unpack.example_or_place: Top of blue grouped phloem drawing.
unpack.consequence: Reinforces the neighbouring-cell relationship.
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse a narrow neighbouring cell with a tube partition.

p011-i35.content: sieve-tube element — leader points to a broad blue cell in the grouped phloem drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: What broad cell is labelled in the grouped view?
teacher_understanding.answer: A sieve-tube element.

teacher_understanding.question: Which structure separates successive elements?
teacher_understanding.answer: The drawing labels a sieve plate at their junction.

teacher_understanding.question: How do elements contribute to a long-distance route?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their end-to-end arrangement forms a sieve tube through which food-containing sap moves.

p011-i35.exam_note: Identify the main conducting cell rather than its neighbour.

unpack.example_or_place: Broad blue grouped phloem cells.
unpack.consequence: A longitudinal route is assembled from several cells.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish element, tube and plate.

p011-i36.content: sieve plate — leader points to the transverse junction between sieve-tube elements.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this transverse label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: A sieve plate between sieve-tube elements.

teacher_understanding.question: Which view also shows a sieve plate?
teacher_understanding.answer: The isolated sieve-tube element to the left.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a partition permit transport?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its pores allow sap to pass across the junction instead of creating a completely sealed barrier.

p011-i36.exam_note: Perforated junction, not a separate tube cell.

unpack.example_or_place: Cross-junction in grouped phloem.
unpack.consequence: A visible division does not imply an impermeable wall.
unpack.level_extra: Compare with pits on xylem side walls.

p011-i37.content: phloem parenchyma cells — leader points to cells beside the grouped sieve-tube elements.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the lower-left label name?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem parenchyma cells in the grouped view.

teacher_understanding.question: Which other phloem cell types appear alongside them?
teacher_understanding.answer: The drawing labels companion cells and sieve-tube elements.

teacher_understanding.question: Why retain a separate label for parenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Associated storage cells and companion cells have different roles, even though both occur next to conducting elements.

p011-i37.exam_note: Do not merge all associated cells into companion cells.

unpack.example_or_place: Lower-left side of grouped phloem.
unpack.consequence: Makes cell-type diversity visible.
unpack.level_extra: Use labels, not merely position, for identification.

p011-i38.content: plasmo-desmata [plasmodesmata] — leader points to fine connections between neighbouring phloem cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What fine connections are labelled?
teacher_understanding.answer: Plasmodesmata linking neighbouring cells in the phloem illustration.

teacher_understanding.question: Which kind of connection does the term refer to?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cytoplasmic channels across cell walls between neighbouring living plant cells.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these connections help coordinated function?
teacher_understanding.answer: They allow substances and signals to move directly between adjacent living cells.

p011-i38.exam_note: Recognise cell-to-cell connections; do not confuse them with sieve plates.

terms.plain_meaning: पास के living plant cells को जोड़ने वाले बारीक रास्ते
terms.everyday_image: दो कमरों के बीच छोटी जोड़ने वाली सुरंगें

why_chain.step: Neighbouring living cells need to exchange substances and information.
Plasmodesmata provide direct connections through their walls.

unpack.example_or_place: Fine connections in the grouped phloem view.
unpack.consequence: Cell walls do not make living plant cells completely isolated.
unpack.level_extra: Keep the term recognisable without adding molecular detail.

p011-i39.content: • Xylem consists of tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres.

teacher_understanding.question: What four components make up xylem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres.

teacher_understanding.question: Where can these components be identified on this page?
teacher_understanding.answer: All four are named in the upper xylem diagram; the lower illustration enlarges conducting elements and parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How are their jobs divided according to the page?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tracheids and vessels conduct water and minerals, parenchyma stores food and conducts water sideways, and fibres mainly support.

p011-i39.exam_note: Four-component list is central to matching and odd-one-out questions.

terms.plain_meaning: इन अलग-अलग हिस्सों से मिलकर बना है
terms.everyday_image: एक टीम में अलग काम वाले सदस्य

why_chain.step: A functioning transport tissue needs conduits, storage and reinforcement.
Xylem divides these roles among its four components.

unpack.example_or_place: Both xylem illustrations.
unpack.consequence: Xylem is a tissue, not the name of one cell type.
unpack.level_extra: Companion cells and sieve tubes are phloem distractors.

p011-i40.content: • Tracheids and vessels have thick walls, and many are dead cells when mature.

teacher_understanding.question: What mature features of the conducting elements are stated?
teacher_understanding.answer: They have thick walls, and the page says many are dead when mature.

teacher_understanding.question: Where are these thick-walled elements located?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are conducting components of xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are thick walls and loss of living contents useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: Thick lignified walls resist collapse, while loss of the protoplast leaves a low-resistance pathway for water movement.

teacher_understanding.question: Does this mean the whole of xylem is dead?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Xylem parenchyma is living; the conventional description of mature tracheids and vessel elements is that they are dead.

p011-i40.exam_note: Avoid 'all xylem cells are dead'; preserve the page's word 'many'.

terms.plain_meaning: अपना पूरा आकार और खास काम करने की अवस्था में पहुँचा हुआ
terms.everyday_image: बनकर इस्तेमाल के लिए तैयार पाइप

why_chain.step: Water pathways must remain open and resist collapse.
Strong walls and an empty mature interior support this conducting role.

unpack.example_or_place: Mature xylem tracheids and vessel elements.
unpack.consequence: Conducting dead cells can coexist with living parenchyma in one tissue.
unpack.visual_verb: clear the interior, retain the wall
unpack.level_extra: Differentiate component-level statements from whole-tissue statements.

p011-i41.content: • Tracheids and vessels are tubular structures. This allows them to transport water and minerals vertically.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the page connect tubular form with conduction?
teacher_understanding.answer: The tube-like structure allows water and minerals to be transported vertically.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these cells form a route through a plant?
teacher_understanding.answer: Vessel elements join end to end, while overlapping tracheids transfer water through pits, producing connected longitudinal pathways.

teacher_understanding.question: Does tube shape alone explain why water rises?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Tube shape provides the route; transpiration pull and the cohesion of water are major contributors to upward movement.

p011-i41.exam_note: Relate shape to vertical conduction; do not equate the route with the driving force.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे की लंबाई की दिशा में, ऊपर की ओर जाने वाला रास्ता
terms.everyday_image: ज़मीन से ऊपर की मंज़िल तक जाती पानी की पाइप

why_chain.step: Water absorbed below must reach leaves above.
Tubular xylem elements provide longitudinal water-and-mineral pathways.

unpack.example_or_place: From root through stem toward leaves.
unpack.consequence: Vertical conduction contrasts with the sideways movement described next.
unpack.level_extra: This is structure–function reasoning, not a complete mechanism of ascent of sap.

p011-i42.content: • The parenchyma stores food and help [helps] in sideways conduction of water.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does xylem need more than vertical conducting elements?
teacher_understanding.answer: Water must also be distributed laterally to neighbouring tissues, and stored food can support local needs.

teacher_understanding.question: How does xylem parenchyma contribute according to the page?
teacher_understanding.answer: It stores food and helps in sideways conduction of water.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this differ from tracheids and vessels?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their stated role is vertical transport of water and minerals, whereas parenchyma adds storage and sideways water movement.

p011-i42.exam_note: Food storage in xylem is not the same as phloem's long-distance food transport.

terms.plain_meaning: पानी को बगल के हिस्सों तक पहुँचाना
terms.everyday_image: मुख्य पाइप से बगल के कमरे में जाती शाखा

why_chain.step: A main upward route alone does not supply all neighbouring cells.
Parenchyma helps sideways conduction and also stores food.

unpack.example_or_place: Xylem parenchyma alongside conducting elements.
unpack.consequence: Water distribution has both longitudinal and lateral components.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid the trap that any mention of food makes a cell part of phloem.

p011-i43.content: • Xylem fibres are mainly supportive in function.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are supportive fibres useful in xylem?
teacher_understanding.answer: The tissue must withstand mechanical stresses while maintaining its conducting framework.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the page distinguish the fibre role?
teacher_understanding.answer: It identifies fibres as mainly supportive, unlike the conducting role assigned to tracheids and vessels.

teacher_understanding.question: How do fibres provide that support?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their thick, lignified walls reinforce the tissue against deformation.

p011-i43.exam_note: Match fibres–support, parenchyma–storage/lateral conduction, tracheids and vessels–conduction.

terms.plain_meaning: ढाँचे को टिकाए रखने और मज़बूत बनाने वाला
terms.everyday_image: पानी की पाइप को थामे रखने वाला मज़बूत सहारा

why_chain.step: A transport framework must resist bending and damage.
Xylem fibres provide mainly mechanical support.

unpack.example_or_place: Fibres within the xylem bundle.
unpack.consequence: Completes the division of labour among the four xylem components.
unpack.level_extra: Retain 'mainly': the page states the principal role, not an absolute exclusion.

p012-i1.content: Phloem is made up of five types of cells: sieve cells, sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibres and the phloem parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: Which five components does the book include in phloem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sieve cells, sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibres and phloem parenchyma form the book's five-part list.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these components differ in their main roles?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sieve elements conduct food; companion cells assist sieve tubes; parenchyma stores materials; fibres provide support. Sieve cells and sieve tubes represent different kinds of conducting elements, not a compulsory pair in every plant.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a conducting tissue contain several cell types?
teacher_understanding.answer: Moving food needs conducting passages, living support and storage, while the plant also needs reinforcement; different cells share these tasks.

p012-i1.exam_note: Learn the component list and avoid assuming every listed type occurs together in every plant.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे में बना खाना पहुँचाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: रसोई से अलग-अलग कमरों तक खाना पहुँचाने की व्यवस्था

why_chain.step: Leaves make food, but other parts also need it.
Phloem combines conducting and supporting cell types to serve that need.

unpack.example_or_place: Vascular tissues in a stem.
unpack.consequence: A complex tissue is not a collection of identical cells.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish a general component list from universal co-occurrence.

p012-i2.content: Sieve tubes are tubular cells with perforated walls.

teacher_understanding.question: What do tubular and perforated mean here?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tubular means elongated like a pipe; perforated means having openings rather than forming an uninterrupted barrier.

teacher_understanding.question: Where are sieve tubes located?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are included among the cell types of phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How do perforations help transport?
teacher_understanding.answer: Openings in sieve plates between neighbouring sieve-tube elements allow food-containing sap to pass along the conducting pathway.

p012-i2.exam_note: Connect perforated sieve plates with food conduction.

terms.plain_meaning: ऐसी दीवारें जिनमें छोटे रास्ते या छेद हों
terms.everyday_image: छन्नी में छेद होते हैं जिनसे चीज़ें पार जा सकती हैं

why_chain.step: Food sap must pass between successive conducting cells.
Perforated end walls provide connecting openings.

unpack.example_or_place: Sieve tubes in stem phloem.
unpack.consequence: Shape and wall openings support conduction.
unpack.visual_verb: pass sap through perforated end plates
unpack.level_extra: Do not interpret this as holes throughout every wall.

p012-i3.content: Phloem transports food from leaves to other parts of the plant.
p012-i3.type_note: This states a transport function, not the spatial arrangement of plant parts.

teacher_understanding.question: What material does phloem distribute?
teacher_understanding.answer: It carries food from leaves to other plant parts.

teacher_understanding.question: What else on this page reinforces that function?
teacher_understanding.answer: The comparison table says phloem carries food materials from leaves to growing parts.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must food leave the leaves?
teacher_understanding.answer: Roots, developing shoots and other consuming or storage regions need sugars even when they do not make enough themselves.

p012-i3.exam_note: Food transport is the key contrast with xylem; do not infer exclusively downward transport.

terms.plain_meaning: बना हुआ खाना दूसरी जगह पहुँचाता है
terms.everyday_image: रसोई का खाना खाने वालों तक पहुँचाना

why_chain.step: Non-photosynthetic and growing regions require food.
Phloem carries food from leaves to other parts.

unpack.example_or_place: Food supply to growing roots.
unpack.consequence: Food production and food use can occur in different places.
unpack.visual_verb: send food arrows from a leaf to growing regions
unpack.level_extra: Source-to-sink transport can occur in different directions in different tubes.

p012-i4.content: Comparison table with columns S.No., Xylem and Phloem; six rows compare transported material, living/dead cells, wall thickness, permeability, wall material and mechanical strength.

p012-i5.content: S.No.: 1. | Xylem: It carries water and minerals from roots to leaves. | Phloem: It carries food materials from the leaves to the growing parts of the plant.

teacher_understanding.question: What transport contrast does the row make?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem supplies water and minerals from roots towards leaves; phloem supplies food from leaves to growing regions.

teacher_understanding.question: How do the transported materials differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Water and mineral ions are not the manufactured sugars carried in food sap.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are separate transport functions useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: Roots obtain water and minerals while photosynthetic leaves manufacture sugars; the plant must connect these different supply points with regions of demand.

p012-i5.exam_note: Common reversal trap: water/minerals versus food.

terms.plain_meaning: जड़ों से पानी और minerals पहुँचाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: पानी ऊपर पहुँचाने वाली पाइप

why_chain.step: Leaves need root-supplied water and growing parts need leaf-made food.
Xylem and phloem serve these distinct supply needs.

unpack.example_or_place: Root–stem–leaf transport.
unpack.consequence: Identify tissue by cargo, not merely arrow direction.
unpack.visual_verb: contrast water arrows with food arrows
unpack.level_extra: Phloem is not defined as downward-only.

p012-i6.content: S.No.: 2. | Xylem: It is composed of dead cells. | Phloem: It is composed of living cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What broad contrast does the book present?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table associates xylem with dead cells and phloem with living cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What qualification prevents an incorrect absolute statement?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem parenchyma is living; phloem fibres are generally dead. The contrast describes the dominant conducting-cell condition rather than every component.

teacher_understanding.question: How can dead cells conduct water?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mature vessel elements and tracheids retain wall-bounded spaces that allow water passage without living cell contents.

p012-i6.exam_note: High-value exceptions: xylem parenchyma and phloem fibres.

terms.plain_meaning: जिनमें जीवित अंदरूनी हिस्सा नहीं बचा
terms.everyday_image: खाली पाइप की दीवार बनी रहती है

why_chain.step: Water requires a continuous conducting route.
Dead mature xylem conducting elements retain passages; living phloem participates in food transport.

unpack.example_or_place: Mature xylem vessels.
unpack.consequence: Avoid converting a broad contrast into an all-cell rule.
unpack.visual_verb: empty a xylem lumen and highlight living phloem
unpack.level_extra: Apply the explicit phloem-fibre exception below the table.

p012-i7.content: S.No.: 3. | Xylem: It has a thick cell wall. | Phloem: It has a thin cell wall.

teacher_understanding.question: What wall-thickness contrast is printed?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem is described as thick-walled and phloem as thin-walled.

teacher_understanding.question: How should this contrast be applied?
teacher_understanding.answer: It principally contrasts conducting elements; phloem fibres have thick walls, so it is not universal across every component.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are strong xylem walls useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: They help conducting passages resist collapse under water tension and reinforce the plant.

p012-i7.exam_note: Remember thick-walled phloem fibres as a qualification.

terms.plain_meaning: cell के चारों ओर मोटी मजबूत दीवार
terms.everyday_image: पतली नली की जगह मजबूत पाइप

why_chain.step: Water-conducting passages must resist collapse.
Thick reinforced walls help preserve their shape.

unpack.example_or_place: Xylem vessels in a stem.
unpack.consequence: Wall thickness links transport with support.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish conducting elements from fibres.

p012-i8.content: S.No.: 4. | Xylem: Its cells are impermeable to the water. | Phloem: Its cells are permeable to food components.

teacher_understanding.question: Which permeability contrast does the table state?
teacher_understanding.answer: It describes xylem cells as impermeable to water and phloem cells as permeable to food components.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must this wording not be read as a complete transport explanation?
teacher_understanding.answer: Water travels through xylem lumens and passes between elements through pits or perforations. Lignified walls do not mean that xylem as a pathway blocks water; phloem transfer is also regulated rather than unrestricted leakage.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a reinforced tube carry water despite resistant walls?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its hollow interior provides a route along the tube; wall properties and passage along the lumen are different issues.

p012-i8.exam_note: Potentially misleading wording: distinguish wall resistance from water conduction.

terms.plain_meaning: जिसके आर-पार आसानी से न जा सके
terms.everyday_image: पाइप की दीवार पानी रोकती है, भीतर का रास्ता पानी ले जाता है

why_chain.step: A transport passage must carry material without being confused with its side wall.
Xylem water passage uses lumens and connecting openings.

unpack.example_or_place: Water inside a vessel lumen.
unpack.consequence: Do not conclude that xylem prevents water transport.
unpack.visual_verb: separate across-wall movement from along-tube movement
unpack.level_extra: Flag this as a simplified textbook contrast.

p012-i9.content: S.No.: 5. | Xylem: Its cells are made up of lignin. | Phloem: Its cells are made up of cellulose.

teacher_understanding.question: Which materials does the book contrast?
teacher_understanding.answer: It associates xylem with lignin and phloem with cellulose.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the accurate distinction behind this shorthand?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem conducting-element walls are reinforced with lignin as well as containing cellulose; cellulose is not exclusive to phloem. The cells themselves are not made solely of one of these substances.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does lignin matter?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lignin stiffens walls and makes them more resistant to collapse, supporting both conduction and mechanical strength.

p012-i9.exam_note: Lignification, not exclusive possession of cellulose, is the meaningful contrast.

terms.plain_meaning: दीवार को कड़ा और मजबूत बनाने वाला substance
terms.everyday_image: लकड़ी की सख्ती

terms.plain_meaning: plant cell की दीवार का मुख्य ढाँचा बनाने वाला substance
terms.everyday_image: कपास के रेशे

why_chain.step: Water-conducting walls need reinforcement.
Lignin strengthens their cellulose-containing walls.

unpack.example_or_place: Woody xylem.
unpack.consequence: Wall composition helps explain thickness and support.
unpack.visual_verb: reinforce a cellulose wall with lignin
unpack.level_extra: Reject 'xylem contains no cellulose'.

p012-i10.content: S.No.: 6. | Xylem: It gives mechanical strength to the plants. | Phloem: Phloem does not give mechanical strength

teacher_understanding.question: What support contrast is printed?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table assigns mechanical strength to xylem and denies it to phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: What exception qualifies the phloem statement?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem fibres provide mechanical support, so the printed denial should not be applied to every phloem component.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does xylem reinforce a plant?
teacher_understanding.answer: Thick lignified walls resist deformation and act as structural reinforcement.

p012-i10.exam_note: Phloem fibres are the important qualification to the absolute wording.

terms.plain_meaning: भार और झुकाव सहकर आकार बनाए रखने की ताकत
terms.everyday_image: इमारत का मजबूत ढाँचा

why_chain.step: A plant must remain upright while carrying leaves and branches.
Reinforced xylem and supporting fibres help bear those loads.

unpack.example_or_place: A woody stem.
unpack.consequence: Transport tissue can also have a supporting role.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid the absolute claim that no phloem component supports.

p012-i11.content: A stem segment labels epidermis, cortex, pith, cambium, xylem and phloem. A red curved arrow enlarges a vascular region into a longitudinal view: xylem at left, cambium in the middle, phloem at right. Black arrows rise within xylem; the illustrated phloem arrows descend. Xylem shows elongated tubes with wall thickening and open connections; phloem shows stacked conducting elements with perforated end regions and adjacent narrow cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What relationship does the enlargement show?
teacher_understanding.answer: The red arrow connects the stem's vascular region to a magnified view of xylem, cambium and phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which directions are drawn?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem arrows point upward and the phloem arrows shown point downward.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the phloem arrows be interpreted?
teacher_understanding.answer: They depict one transport direction, not a universal restriction. Phloem carries material from a source to a sink, which may lie above or below it.

p012-i11.exam_note: Identify inner xylem, intervening cambium and outer phloem.

terms.plain_meaning: xylem और phloem के बीच नई cells बनाने वाली परत
terms.everyday_image: दो हिस्सों के बीच नई ईंटें जोड़ने वाली पट्टी

why_chain.step: A small vascular region is difficult to distinguish in the whole stem.
The enlarged view separates its conducting and growing regions.

unpack.example_or_place: The stem shown beside the table.
unpack.consequence: Spatial arrangement can be linked with transport function.
unpack.visual_verb: zoom into the vascular region and animate arrows
unpack.level_extra: The red arrow means enlargement, not sap movement.

p012-i12.content: epidermis — points to the outer surface layer of the stem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does epidermis identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The outer covering of the small stem drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: Which labelled region lies farther inward?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cortex lies beneath the epidermis.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is an outer covering useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: It protects internal tissues and helps limit unwanted water loss.

terms.plain_meaning: सबसे बाहर की ढकने वाली परत
terms.everyday_image: फल का बाहरी छिलका

unpack.example_or_place: Stem surface.
unpack.consequence: Locates the boundary before moving inward.

p012-i13.content: cortex — points to tissue beneath the epidermis and outside the vascular region.

teacher_understanding.question: What region is labelled cortex?
teacher_understanding.answer: The peripheral tissue inside the stem's outer covering.

teacher_understanding.question: Which position distinguishes it from pith?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cortex is toward the outside of the vascular tissues; pith occupies the central region.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this help read the diagram?
teacher_understanding.answer: It provides an outer landmark for locating the deeper vascular tissues.

p012-i13.exam_note: Use cortex as an outer positional landmark.

terms.plain_meaning: बाहरी परत के नीचे का हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: छिलके के अंदर की पट्टी

unpack.example_or_place: Peripheral stem tissue.
unpack.consequence: Separates outer tissue from central pith.

p012-i14.content: pith — points to the central internal region of the stem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does pith name in this drawing?
teacher_understanding.answer: The stem's central internal region.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue is nearer the pith: xylem or phloem?
teacher_understanding.answer: In this arrangement, xylem lies on the inner side toward the pith.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the pith label orient the learner?
teacher_understanding.answer: It establishes the centre, allowing inner xylem to be distinguished from outer phloem.

p012-i14.exam_note: Central landmark, not a conducting-tissue label.

terms.plain_meaning: तने के बीच का अंदरूनी हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: गोल चीज़ का बीच वाला भाग

unpack.example_or_place: Centre of the illustrated stem.
unpack.consequence: Helps orient the vascular arrangement.

p012-i15.content: cambium — points to the layer between xylem and phloem in the vascular region.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this cambium label locate?
teacher_understanding.answer: The intervening region between the two conducting tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Which meristem category includes vascular cambium?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a lateral meristem associated with secondary growth.

teacher_understanding.question: How does it increase stem girth?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its divisions produce secondary xylem inward and secondary phloem outward.

p012-i15.exam_note: Links the diagram with lateral meristem in the practice question.

terms.plain_meaning: नई cells बनाकर मोटाई बढ़ाने वाली परत
terms.everyday_image: दीवार में नई कतारें जोड़ना

unpack.example_or_place: Between xylem and phloem.
unpack.consequence: Connects tissue location with growth in girth.
unpack.level_extra: Vascular cambium is a lateral meristem.

p012-i16.content: xylem — points to the inner conducting region of the small stem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this xylem label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The inner conducting region selected for enlargement.

teacher_understanding.question: Which cargo belongs to this tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table assigns water and minerals to xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How can it be distinguished spatially from phloem?
teacher_understanding.answer: In this stem arrangement, it lies inward of cambium while phloem is outward.

terms.plain_meaning: पानी और minerals ले जाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: भीतर की पानी वाली पाइप

unpack.example_or_place: Inner side of the vascular region.
unpack.consequence: Connects the whole stem with the enlargement.
unpack.visual_verb: trace xylem into the enlarged view

p012-i17.content: phloem — points to the outer conducting region of the small stem.

teacher_understanding.question: What region does this phloem label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The outer conducting region shown beside the xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which transported material identifies phloem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Food from leaves is assigned to phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does location help distinguish it?
teacher_understanding.answer: In this arrangement, phloem lies outside cambium rather than toward the pith.

terms.plain_meaning: बना खाना पहुँचाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: खाना पहुँचाने का रास्ता

unpack.example_or_place: Outer vascular region.
unpack.consequence: Identifies the food-conducting side.

p012-i18.content: xylem — brackets the left-hand thickened conducting tubes with upward arrows.

teacher_understanding.question: What structures are grouped under xylem?
teacher_understanding.answer: The enlarged left-hand elongated conducting structures.

teacher_understanding.question: Which direction is shown within them?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their black arrows point upward.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the wall pattern relate to function?
teacher_understanding.answer: Wall reinforcement helps maintain open water-conducting passages.

p012-i18.exam_note: Identify xylem from thickened walls and upward water pathway.

why_chain.step: Water pathways must remain open.
Reinforced walls resist collapse.

unpack.example_or_place: Left side of the enlargement.
unpack.consequence: Links microscopic structure with table contrasts.

p012-i19.content: cambium — brackets the narrow central cell region separating xylem and phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the enlarged cambium label group?
teacher_understanding.answer: The narrow central region between the two conducting tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissues border it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem borders its left side and phloem its right side in the enlargement.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this location significant?
teacher_understanding.answer: A dividing layer here can add vascular tissue to both sides during secondary growth.

p012-i19.exam_note: Recognise cambium by its intervening position.

why_chain.step: A thickening stem needs additional conducting tissue.
Cambium adds xylem and phloem on opposite sides.

unpack.example_or_place: Middle strip of the enlargement.
unpack.consequence: Explains the lateral-growth connection.
unpack.visual_verb: expand the central strip into new rows

p012-i20.content: phloem — brackets the right-hand conducting region with perforated end regions and downward arrows.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the enlarged phloem label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The right-hand food-conducting region adjacent to cambium.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visible feature connects with the sieve-tube bullet?
teacher_understanding.answer: The conducting elements show perforated end regions.

teacher_understanding.question: How should its downward arrows be taught?
teacher_understanding.answer: As the illustrated direction of food movement, not proof that phloem transport is exclusively downward.

p012-i20.exam_note: Arrow direction is illustrative, not an absolute rule.

why_chain.step: Food must pass between adjoining conducting elements.
Perforated sieve plates provide connecting routes.

unpack.example_or_place: Right side of the enlargement.
unpack.consequence: Connects sieve-tube structure with food movement.
unpack.level_extra: Source and sink determine direction.

p012-i21.content: Except phloem fibres, other phloem cells are living cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which phloem component is the stated exception?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem fibres are excluded from the statement that phloem cells are living.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this line qualify the table?
teacher_understanding.answer: It explicitly adds an exception to the table's broad description of phloem as composed of living cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can fibres function after losing living contents?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their supporting role depends mainly on strong walls rather than continuing metabolism.

terms.plain_meaning: phloem के मजबूत सहारा देने वाले लंबे हिस्से
terms.everyday_image: रस्सी के मजबूत रेशे

why_chain.step: A plant needs structural support as well as food movement.
Fibre walls can provide support without living contents at maturity.

unpack.example_or_place: Fibres associated with phloem.
unpack.consequence: The word 'all' makes a living-phloem statement unsafe.
unpack.visual_verb: single out the fibre from living components
unpack.level_extra: Living sieve-tube elements lack a nucleus at maturity; absence of a nucleus alone does not mean dead.

p012-i22.content: Q. Fat present below the skin surface in our body, acts as a barrier against: (HPAS 2020)
p012-i22.type_note: 2020 identifies the examination year; this is a biological function question, not a timeline.

teacher_understanding.question: Which option answers the question?
